items.title: U.S.-Russia Talks on Ukraine Involve Multi-Billion Dollar Oil Deal, NYT Reports
items.summary: Putin reportedly raised the deal during a Sept. 5 meeting with Witkoff and Kushner at the Kremlin.
items.body_text:
The Trump administration’s talks with Russia on ending the war in Ukraine have expanded to include a multibillion-dollar oil deal that would benefit Middle Eastern business executives with ties to U.S. negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, the New York Times reported on Saturday.
The deal, which is contingent on approval from the U.S. government and the Kremlin, involves a sprawling set of oil fields, refineries and gas stations around the world owned by Russian energy group Lukoil, according to the report.
The White House, the U.S. Treasury Department and Lukoil didn't respond to requests for comment outside regular business hours.
The group pursuing the deal includes U.S. investor and billionaire Todd Boehly, two Middle Eastern groups that have done business with Kushner or Witkoff's family, and an arm of the U.S. government, the newspaper said.
Russian President Vladimir Putin raised the deal during a Sept. 5 meeting with Witkoff and Kushner at the Kremlin, the NYT said citing people familiar with the meeting. Putin proposed completing the deal as a way to show Russians they could do business with the United States, one of the people said.

items.title: Ex-Deputy Governor Who Planned to Fight in Ukraine Gets 14 Years for Military Supplies Theft
items.summary: Alexander Vlasov, who also headed the Kuban Cossack Host, was arrested one day after he resigned in order to fight in Ukraine.
items.body_text:
A Russian court sentenced a former deputy governor of the southern Krasnodar region to 14 years in prison for abuse of authority and organizing the theft of supplies intended for troops fighting in Ukraine, the regional courts’ press service said.
Vlasov resigned as deputy governor of Krasnodar in September 2025 and announced plans to join the Kuban brigade fighting in Ukraine. He was arrested the following day.
Vlasov, who also headed the Kuban Cossack Host, was fined 1 million rubles ($11,900) and barred from holding managerial or administrative positions in state or local government for three years.
His adviser, Alexander Starodubtsev, received six years for fraud, the same fine and a two-and-a-half-year employment ban. Both men will serve their sentences in general-regime penal colonies.
The verdict has yet to take legal effect.
The Sovetsky District Court in Krasnodar found that the Cossack organization received a 100 million ruble ($1.19 million) government subsidy in August 2022 to buy supplies for BARS-1, BARS-11, BARS-16 and other units fighting in Ukraine.
It bought uniforms, protective gear and other equipment worth 57.75 million rubles ($687,225) between August and December that year but failed to deliver them by the deadline.
Acting on Vlasov’s instructions, Starodubtsev stole goods worth about 2.31 million rubles ($27,489) with the intention of selling them through an online classifieds website, the court found.
Belts, gloves, raincoats, boots and socks were advertised on Avito, the local outlet Za Krasnodar reported in September. Investigators recovered stolen goods from Starodubtsev’s home, it said.
In early 2023, Starodubtsev also took goods worth 347,868 rubles ($4,140) that had been incorrectly recorded as delivered. He kept them at home awaiting buyers until law enforcement officers seized them, according to the court statement reported by Kubanskie Novosti.
Vlasov instructed employees of the Cossack organization and representatives of military units to falsify delivery records to conceal the theft, the court found.
One BARS member testified that, at Vlasov’s instruction, he signed a delivery document for about 20 million rubles ($238,000) worth of goods despite receiving none of them, according to case materials published by Za Krasnodar.
The witness, whose testimony was read out in court because he was in the combat zone, said shortages of uniforms, drones and other equipment prevented units from fully carrying out combat tasks.
Kommersant reported in August that commanders and military representatives also described receiving fewer supplies than records showed. The organization’s former chief accountant testified that she handled paperwork without monitoring deliveries.
Vlasov became deputy governor of Krasnodar in September 2020 and took over the Kuban Cossack Host in 2021.

items.title: Lukashenko Vows Belarus’ Full Support for Putin on Ukraine
items.summary: The comments come as Belarus has been attempting to improve ties with the United States after years of isolation and Western sanctions.
items.body_text:
Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko reaffirmed his alignment with Russia over its war in Ukraine on Friday, despite highlighting nuances in his own perspective on the conflict.
His comments follow Belarus’ efforts to improve ties with the United States after years of isolation and Western sanctions. U.S. President Donald Trump's administration has reopened a dialogue with Minsk, easing some sanctions in exchange for prisoner releases.
“I told [Russian] President [Vladimir] Putin openly: I have my own understanding of certain aspects of the conflict in Ukraine, but we’ll always remain committed to our common course,” Lukashenko said, according to the state news agency Belta.
“If you, the Russian leadership, make a decision, we’ll always be with you despite our particular ways of understanding what’s happening there. We’ve never been traitors,” Lukashenko added.
He spoke at a gathering of the governing body of the Eurasian Economic Union, a Russian-led bloc, which includes Armenia, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan alongside Belarus.
Twice this year, the president of Kazakhstan has proposed freezing the conflict to restart diplomatic talks.
Lukashenko said that he, like Putin, knows the situation on the front lines in Ukraine, which he claimed allows them both to maintain “more refined approaches” to the war.
Belarus allowed Moscow to use its territory as a staging ground for the 2022 invasion of Ukraine, but Lukashenko has said that Belarusian troops would not be sent directly into the war. At the same time, he has intensified military preparations with the deployment of Russia’s nuclear-capable Oreshnik hypersonic ballistic missile system and announced a “targeted mobilization” of Belarusian forces.
Belarus has also sought to have U.S. sanctions lifted since Donald Trump returned to the White House last year. The Biden administration had introduced many of the sanctions in response to the 2020 election crackdown in Belarus and Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

items.body_text:
Russian forces strike a second major Kyiv bridge across the Dnipro after two days of attacks on the South Bridge
Russian forces struck Kyiv’s Northern Bridge on the morning of October 3, damaging the road surface and overhead trolleybus power lines. Mayor Vitali Klitschko said the bridge was partially closed to traffic.
On October 1 and 2, Russia carried out at least three drone attacks on Kyiv’s Southern Bridge, damaging a support, a guardrail, the road surface, and the metro’s protective concrete barrier. The bridge was closed to all traffic.
BBC Ukrainian reported that these were the first strikes of the war on Kyiv’s bridges across the Dnipro River.
Kyiv has nine bridges across the Dnipro, carrying road, pedestrian, and rail traffic. The Northern and Southern bridges are among the busiest and most important river crossings. In the preceding days, strikes on the two bridges also prompted partial traffic closures on other Kyiv bridges. Traffic jams formed in the city.

items.title: Russian guard and inmate killed aboard train carrying prisoners. Reports conflict over alleged riot.
items.summary: A prisoner being transferred attacked his guards aboard a Vladikavkaz–Adler train in Kabardino-Balkaria, RBC, Interfax, and TASS reported, citing law enforcement sources.
items.body_text:
Russian guard and inmate killed aboard train carrying prisoners. Reports conflict over alleged riot.
A prisoner being transferred attacked his guards aboard a Vladikavkaz–Adler train in Kabardino-Balkaria, RBC, Interfax, and TASS reported, citing law enforcement sources.
The sources said the prisoner grabbed a guard’s weapon while being escorted to the bathroom and opened fire on officers from Russia’s prison service, the Federal Penitentiary Service (FSIN). One officer later died on the way to the hospital, and three others were wounded.
The guards killed the prisoner when they returned fire, the sources said.
REN TV and the Telegram channel 112 initially reported that prisoners had rioted on the train. Sources cited by both outlets said the prisoners had killed one guard and taken three wounded guards hostage.
Later, an FSIN source told TASS that the reports of a riot were “not true.”
There were 15 prisoners in the railcar, Mash reported.

items.title: Canadian who moved his family to Russia for ‘traditional values’ says he no longer recommends it: permanent residency would require signing a Defense Ministry contract
items.summary: Canadian farmer Arend Feenstra, who moved to Russia through a streamlined immigration program for citizens of “unfriendly” countries who share “traditional values,” has complained that he cannot get a permanent residence permit. The news outlet Nizhny Novgorod Onlain drew attention to his YouTube video.
items.body_text:
Canadian who moved his family to Russia for ‘traditional values’ says he no longer recommends it: permanent residency would require signing a Defense Ministry contract
Canadian farmer Arend Feenstra, who moved to Russia through a streamlined immigration program for citizens of “unfriendly” countries who share “traditional values,” has complained that he cannot get a permanent residence permit. The news outlet Nizhny Novgorod Onlain drew attention to his YouTube video.
Feenstra received a three-year temporary residence permit in Russia’s Nizhny Novgorod region in early 2025. He then brought his wife and eight children to Russia and began farming.
But Feenstra has now learned that to replace his temporary residence permit with a permanent one, he must sign a contract with Russia’s Defense Ministry.
We’ve already […] grown attached to this place. I didn’t come here to sign a contract. I understand what it’s for and why [the authorities] want you to sign it. But I have eight young children at home and a farm. […] In that case, I’d rather take my chances in Canada, though I think living there is risky too.
Feenstra said that once his current temporary residence permit expires, he will be able to apply for temporary residence again without signing a contract. He also said his family no longer recommends that other foreigners move to Russia because the authorities keep changing the rules and “there’s no way forward.”
The program, launched in August 2024, encourages foreigners from “unfriendly” countries who share “traditional Russian spiritual and moral values” to immigrate to Russia. Participants receive temporary residence permits through a simplified application process that, among other things, does not require them to take Russian-language exams.
Since November 2025, foreign men ages 18 to 65 who are deemed fit for military service have been required to sign a contract with the Defense Ministry to obtain a permanent residence permit in Russia. People who moved to Russia through the “traditional values” program are not exempt from this requirement.

items.title: India explode in 2nd half, crush Malaysia 5-1 to retain Asian Games gold; seal LA28 spot
items.summary: India had never won successive Asian Games gold medals, making Saturday's final an opportunity to create history. Harmanpreet Singh-led India made the most of it as they successfully defended their title.
items.body_text:
The Indian men's hockey team defended their 
Asian Games
 gold medal and secured a spot at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics after defeating Malaysia 5-1 in the final in Kakamigahara, Japan, on Saturday.
India had never won successive Asian Games gold medals, making Saturday's final an opportunity to create history. Harmanpreet Singh-led India made the most of it as they successfully defended their title.
Malaysia secured the silver, while Pakistan won the bronze by defeating South Korea 5-3 earlier in the day.
India started slowly as Malaysia, as expected, defended in a low block and managed to keep the Indian attack out despite the pressure. India eventually broke the deadlock in the 12th minute through Harmanpreet.
India won their first penalty corner after Hardik played Abhishek into the circle and the forward found a Malaysian defender's foot. Harmanpreet took the first attempt, but the push from Hardik was poor. India, however, won another penalty corner.
Harmanpreet made no mistake with his second chance. The trap was better this time and he beat the first rusher with his drag-flick before sending a powerful shot past the goalkeeper, who could not see it to put India in the lead.
Malaysia responded quickly and equalised just two minutes later in the 14th minute. Shello Silverius thrashed a half volley into the roof of the net from the left end of the circle. He received an aerial ball from the right and got his shot away almost immediately.
The first quarter ended 1-1.
India regained the lead in the 23rd minute through another penalty corner. Shilanand Lakra received the ball on the left wing and found a chance to enter the circle, but the attack was stopped. Soon after, Lakra made another run into the circle and this time won a foul.
Jugraj Singh converted the penalty corner to put India 2-1 ahead.
Malaysia continued to press India and put the defending champions under pressure, but India held on to their lead at half-time.
India extended their advantage in the 42nd minute when Hardik Singh scored from another penalty corner. The goalkeeper moved to his right early, allowing Hardik to place the ball centrally and make it 3-1 for India.
India exerted their dominance in the last few minutes as Abhishek scored another goal for India in the 55th minute to make it 4-1. Harmanpreet followed soon after to score his second goal of the match through penalty corner with a rocket drag-flick flying into the top left of the goal to put India into a comfortable 5-1 lead.
India held on to complete a 5-1 victory over Malaysia and successfully defend their Asian Games title. The triumph came a day after the Indian women's hockey team also won gold, beating China 1-0 in the final, giving India a golden double in hockey.

items.title: Major lapse by Israeli intel? Over 12 Omani pilots flew to Tel Aviv despite ban
items.summary: Israeli passengers, the captain and other pilots on board intervened, allowing the plane to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. Most of the passengers were Israeli and were later flown from Saudi Arabia to Israel. Oman does not have diplomatic relations with Israel. According to the report, rules introduced after 2020 Abraham Accords prohibit pilots from countries that do not have relations with Israel from flying into the country.
items.body_text:
Israeli authorities are facing tough questions over how an Omani pilot was able to fly into Tel Aviv despite a rule barring pilots from countries without diplomatic relations with Israel, according to a report by Channel 12.
The issue came to light after a hijacking attempt was made on a flydubai flight on Wednesday when its Omani co-pilot allegedly attacked the captain, Smit Machchhar, and attempted to deliberately crash the aircraft.
Israeli passengers, the captain and other pilots on board intervened, allowing the plane to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. Most of the passengers were Israeli and were later flown from Saudi Arabia to Israel.
Over 12 Omani pilots flew into Israel
Oman does not have diplomatic relations with Israel. According to the report, rules introduced after the 2020 Abraham Accords prohibit pilots from countries that do not have relations with Israel from flying into the country.
However, Channel 12 reported that dozens of Omani pilots had flown into Israel in recent years while working for foreign airlines.
The report said Israeli authorities had largely relied on airlines themselves to ensure that pilots from countries without diplomatic ties with Israel did not operate flights into the country.
Channel 12 reported that the Shin Bet security service did not independently investigate the nationalities or backgrounds of flydubai pilots. Instead, it had asked the airline not to use pilots from countries that do not have diplomatic relations with Israel.
âThe Shin Bet has all the means to know, within five minutes, who all of the pilots on the Dubai airline are, and they simply chose to turn a blind eye,â the network quoted an anonymous airline industry official as saying. âIn Israel, they expected the airline to be reliable enough, so they didnât conduct reviews in recent years.â
Israel's Transportation Ministry said the Shin Bet had not issued a specific warning about flydubai, apart from requesting increased baggage checks, according to the report.
Security procedures now under scrutiny
The incident has prompted authorities to examine how flight crews from foreign airlines are cleared to enter Israel. Channel 12 reported that the Transportation Ministry and its Center for Aviation Security Operations, which was established in recent years to oversee and monitor the entry of flight crews, will be examined as part of the investigation.
The State Comptroller's Office had already recommended in 2024 that the government review security procedures related to air travel.
The report also pointed to an earlier dispute between the Shin Bet and Israeli airlines El Al, IsraAir and Arkia. In July, the security service barred the three carriers from landing in Dubai because of concerns over regional tensions linked to the war with Iran.
Although that decision involved Israeli airlines rather than foreign carriers, Channel 12 reported that applying similarly strict security measures to foreign airlines could potentially have helped prevent Wednesday's incident.
Investigation points to possible terror motive
Investigations into the attack are continuing in Israel, the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia. The Shin Bet and Mossad are also reportedly cooperating with security agencies in the two countries.
Saudi Arabia said the captain and co-pilot, who were treated in hospital for their injuries, left for Abu Dhabi on Thursday after receiving medical clearance.
Initial information shared with Israeli authorities reportedly suggested that the co-pilot may have attacked for nationalist reasons, raising the possibility that the incident was treated as a terror attack. The assessment was reportedly based partly on statements the co-pilot made to Saudi investigators, along with other information gathered during the probe.
Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu said earlier Thursday that the Omani first officer âunderwent Islamist radical indoctrination.â Channel 12 said that assessment was based on information from two Isra

items.title: 'Dragged to basement, assaulted': 7 held after woman partially stripped at nightclub
items.summary: Seven individuals, including a nightclub manager, were arrested following an incident of assault at The Locals nightclub. The incident occurred after a drunken altercation where a woman was reportedly assaulted by bouncers. Police conducted an investigation after receiving information about the assault and reviewed CCTV footage from the nightclub. A video circulating on social media showed the woman being assaulted, leading to police action.
items.body_text:
GUWAHATI: Seven people, including a nightclub manager, were arrested on Saturday after a woman was allegedly âpartially stripped and assaultedâ by bouncers following a drunken brawl at a bar here a day earlier, police said.
The arrests came after police registered a suo motu case and launched an investigation into the alleged assault at the nightclub in the Khanapara area early on Friday.
The action followed the circulation of a video purportedly showing the incident on social media.
The arrested people, aged between 21 and 30, include three women.
Among them are the nightclub manager, event manager and a front office executive.
Police are also investigating how the nightclub, âThe Localsâ, remained open well beyond its permitted closing time of 12.30am.
Guwahati East deputy police commissioner Tabu Ram Pegu said police launched an inquiry after receiving information about the incident and examined the available CCTV footage.
"The footage revealed that the victim was assaulted inside the bar by a group of people at around 2.30 am. Thereafter, she was dragged towards the basement by pulling her hair and clothes, where she was again assaulted and appeared to become semi-conscious," Tabu told news agency PTI.
Several of those allegedly involved in the incident were associated with the bar or were among its staff, Pegu said, adding that the management did not inform the local police station about the incident.
"Accordingly, a suo motu case was registered at the Dispur police station, and an investigation has been taken up. Seven people have been arrested so far," the DCP said.
Pegu added that the police are examining the complete sequence of events, the role of each individual involved, the operation of the establishment beyond the permitted closing time, and any other violations that may emerge during the investigation.
The video that surfaced online purportedly shows the woman being assaulted while lying on the floor of a buildingâs parking lot. Another woman is later seen intervening and coming to her rescue.
According to a security guard working at the building that houses the club, the woman had hit a female bouncer with a beer bottle inside the club.
"This angered other bouncers there, and they brought her downstairs and assaulted her," he claimed.
(With agency inputs)

items.title: China launches anti-dumping probe into EU chemical imports ahead of trade talks
items.summary: Beijing rejects that its manufacturers' competitiveness is based on state support and has threatened countermeasures against EU moves to block its firms
items.body_text:
China's Commerce Ministry launched an anti-dumping investigation into imports of a widely used production chemical from the European Union on Saturday (October 3, 2026), less than a week before the bloc's trade chief was due in Beijing for talks.
A spokesperson for Beijing's Commerce Ministry said China's domestic industry had requested the investigation into whether imports from the EU of low-priced p-nitrotoluene were flooding the Chinese market, complaining of "damage to production and operations".
The chemical is used in the production of dyes, pharmaceuticals, and pesticides.
Simmering trade tensions between Beijing and Brussels have threatened to become a full-blown trade war as the 27-nation bloc scrambles to defend its industries against a flood of Chinese exports critics argue are supported by vast subsidies.
Beijing rejects that its manufacturers' competitiveness is based on state support and has threatened countermeasures against EU moves to block its firms.
Maros Sefcovic, the EU's trade commissioner, and Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao will hold critical talks on Thursday (October 8, 2026) aimed at avoiding an escalation of tit-for-tat trade measures.
In September, the EU began an investigation into polyvinyl chloride imports from countries including China.
China's newly launched investigation will conclude within 12 months, with the possibility of a six-month extension, the Ministry said.
"China has repeatedly reiterated that the EU needs to face its own economic and trade problems directly and resolve mutual concerns through dialogue and consultation," the spokesperson added.

items.title: FlyDubai co-pilot was Omani national flagged over extremism concerns, sources say
items.summary: The co-pilot has been identified as Hamam al-Hammami, according to three people with knowledge of the situation, including a Gulf and Western diplomat
items.body_text:
The Flydubai co-pilot accused of attacking the captain on an Israel-bound flight with an axe and trying to seize the controls was an Omani national who’d been barred from flying on his country’s airline because of concerns about extremist views, officials said Saturday (OCtober 3, 2026).
The co-pilot has been identified as Hamam al-Hammami, according to three people with knowledge of the situation, including a Gulf and Western diplomat, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to speak to the media.
The United Arab Emirates, which is leading the investigation, said the co-pilot attacked with the cockpit’s crash axe and tried to take control of the sharply plummeting plane in a “terrorist attack” on Wednesday (September 30, 2026). His actions nearly crashed the flight with 182 people on board before passengers and others rushed in and subdued him.
The new details raises questions about how the co-pilot was on the flight. Israel’s government has said it has agreements with foreign carriers to keep pilots of nations without diplomatic ties from flying there. Israel and Oman don’t have formal diplomatic relations.
FlyDubai hired the copilot after Oman Air barred him
Separately, a regional official and a person familiar with the matter said the co-pilot had been barred from flying by Oman over concerns he had adopted extremist views. The official said he was moved to an administrative job at Oman Air. Both spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss the ongoing investigation.
The co-pilot was later hired by UAE-based airline FlyDubai, the person said. It was not immediately clear to what extent the co-pilot was vetted.
The regional official said the co-pilot was born in the UAE and his mother is Syrian. How he obtained Omani nationality was not immediately clear.
The official also said security agencies from four regional countries were working to establish the co-pilot’s motives, aided by the United States and other Western governments.
The Gulf diplomat said investigations were trying to establish whether the co-pilot acted alone or “has any connection with any extremist groups.”
Questions grow over security measures
A FlyDubai spokesperson said in an email that the airline could not comment beyond its official statements and acknowledged “there are many questions at this stage”. There was no immediate comment from Oman Air, and Oman’s government has said nothing publicly in response to repeated questions since the incident.
The incident is a test for the UAE government, which has earned a reputation for effective measures against extremist activities but has also bristled in the past over criticism of security lapses.
Airlines are generally required to carry crash axes in the cockpit that could be used in an emergency to break open a window to escape or break open a panel to access a fire. The axes are generally stored in the cockpits where the crew can reach them, but they aren’t accessible to passengers.
A social media account was deleted the day of the flight
Little else was immediately known about the co-pilot’s background. His Instagram account was active until the day of the flight and then deleted.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Friday (October 2, 2026) said the co-pilot had undergone “Islamist radicalisation”, but provided no evidence. There was no immediate comment on Saturday (October 3, 2026) from Israel’s government.
ALSO WATCH Flydubai incident: What went wrong On Flydubai Flight FZ 1073? Here’s how a mid-air attack unfolded
The Captain, Indian national Smit Machchhar, who was badly wounded, has said he used his remaining energy while being attacked to unlock the cockpit door, allowing people who had noticed alarmingly unusual sounds to come in, tackle the co-pilot and stabilise the flight.
The plane made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia after a descent so extreme that part of the rudder was torn away, and aviation experts have marvelled that it didn’t crash.

राहुल गांधी ने ‘सत्याग्रह’ पहल शुरू की:कहा- लोग अपनी समस्याएं भेजें; महात्मा गांधी ने भी यही तरीका अपनाया था, आज भी 8,500+ लेटर रिकॉर्ड में
- कॉपी लिंक
राहुल गांधी ने देशभर में अन्याय और अपने हक के लिए लड़ रहे लोगों की आवाज को एक साथ जोड़ने के लिए सत्याग्रह नाम से एक पहल शुरू की है।
राहुल ने कहा कि जो भी लोग अन्याय के खिलाफ लड़ रहे हैं, वे अपनी कहानी भेजें। मैं नेता विपक्ष के रूप में संसद से लेकर सड़क तक आपके साथ खड़ा हूं।
राहुल की इस पहल का नाम महात्मा गांधी के ‘सत्याग्रह’ से जुड़ा है। आजादी की लड़ाई के दौरान गांधीजी ने भी यही तरीका अपनाया था। गांधी हेरिटेज पोर्टल के मुताबिक, उस समय लोगों ने गांधीजी को जमीन, संपत्ति, जेल और अन्याय से जुड़े मामलों की जानकारी भेजी थी। गांधीजी को भेजे गए 8,500 से ज्यादा लेटर आज भी मौजूद हैं। हालांकि, वास्तविक संख्या ज्यादा हो सकती है।
राहुल बोले- अकेले लड़ने वालों की आवाज दब जाती है
राहुल गांधी ने X पर लिखा- देशभर में लोग अपने हक के लिए लड़ रहे हैं और अक्सर अकेले लड़ रहे हैं। जेन-जी, छात्र, किसान, आदिवासी, दलित, महिलाएं। हर संघर्ष की अपनी कहानी है। पर जो आवाज अकेली उठती है, वो अक्सर दब जाती है।
सत्याग्रह इन्हीं आवाजों को एक साथ लाने की पहल है। बापू ने यही सिखाया था - सच सबसे बड़ा हथियार है। पर उससे भी बड़ा हथियार है, एकता में सच के साथ खड़े होना। अगर आप भी किसी अन्याय से लड़ रहे हैं - अपनी कहानी भेजिए। दो मिनट लगेंगे।
विपक्ष 6 अक्टूबर को चुनाव आयोग का घेराव करेगा
मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त (CEC) ज्ञानेश कुमार के इस्तीफे की मांग और वोटर लिस्ट के SIR के विरोध में विपक्षी दल, कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी (CJP) और लेफ्ट छात्र संगठन प्रदर्शन कर रहे हैं।
CJP ने शुक्रवार को मुंबई के शिवाजी पार्क में प्रदर्शन किया। वे 10 अक्टूबर को दिल्ली के जंतर-मंतर पर जुटेंगे। वहीं, चुनाव आयुक्त ज्ञानेश कुमार के इस्तीफे की मांग को लेकर कांग्रेस समेत विपक्षी दलों के सांसद 6 अक्टूबर को चुनाव आयोग का घेराव करेंगे।
ज्ञानेश कुमार और चुनाव आयोग का विवाद समझें…
दरअसल, द इंडियन एक्सप्रेस की रिपोर्ट के मुताबिक, दो चुनाव आयुक्तों विवेक जोशी और सुखबीर सिंह संधू ने फॉर्म 6 में बदलाव और SIR से जुड़े फैसलों को लेकर 10 महीने में 14 बार आपत्ति जताई थी। इस रिपोर्ट के आने के बाद CEC ज्ञानेश कुमार के इस्तीफे और पुरानी वोटर लिस्ट पर चुनाव कराने की मांग शुरू हो गई।
दोनों आयुक्तों ने 4 बड़े सवाल उठाए…
1. फॉर्म-6 में बदलाव: नए वोटरों से पिछली SIR लिस्ट में खुद या परिवार के नाम की जानकारी मांगने पर दोनों ने सवाल उठाया। संधू ने इसे गैरकानूनी बताते हुए हटाने की मांग की।
2. वोटर डेटा का कंट्रोल: दोनों ने सवाल किया कि वोटर डेटाबेस का कंट्रोल दिल्ली में क्यों बढ़ रहा है और राज्यों की पहुंच क्यों सीमित हो रही है।
3. बंगाल में 16 लाख अपीलें: संधू ने पूछा कि हटाए गए नामों को लेकर करीब 16 लाख अपीलें किसने और किसकी अनुमति से दायर कीं।
4. गोवा के 97 वोटर: जांच में योग्य पाए गए 97 वोटरों को सॉफ्टवेयर की समस्या के कारण अंतिम लिस्ट में नहीं जोड़ा जा सका।
----------------------------------
ये खबर भी पढ़ें…
मुंबई में ज्ञानेश कुमार के खिलाफ CJP का प्रदर्शन, दीपके बोले- 10 अक्टूबर को कॉकरोच दिल्ली आएंगे
मुंबई के शिवाजी पार्क में कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी ने मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त ज्ञानेश कुमार के इस्तीफे की मांग को लेकर प्रदर्शन किया। पार्टी ने वोटर लिस्ट के SIR को लेकर भी सवाल उठाए। इस दौरान स्टेज पर मौजूद सभी लोग महात्मा गांधी की फोटो वाली टी-शर्ट पहनकर पहुंचे। पूरी खबर पढ़ें…

items.body_text:
- Hindi News
- National
- Rainfall Flood Crisis Situation LIVE Photos Update; UP Bihar Gandak River | MP UP Rajasthan Weather
बिहार का 73% हिस्सा बाढ़ प्रभावित:इस पर सालाना ₹6.4 हजार करोड़ खर्च; यूपी में 15 नदियां उफान पर; MP से मानसून की विदाई
- कॉपी लिंक
बिहार में बाढ़ की स्थिति गंभीर होती जा रही है। बिहार सरकार के मुताबिक, राज्य का करीब 68.80 लाख हेक्टेयर क्षेत्र यानी लगभग 73% हिस्सा बाढ़ प्रभावित है। राज्य के 38 में से 28 जिले बाढ़ की चपेट में आने वाले माने जाते हैं। सरकार हर साल बाढ़ से निपटने और बाढ़ नियंत्रण से जुड़े कामों पर करीब ₹6.4 हजार करोड़ खर्च करती है।
वहीं, बिहार में गंडक नदी में उफान और तटबंध टूटने से सारण समेत 6 जिलों के करीब 255 गांव बाढ़ की चपेट में हैं। इससे करीब 4 लाख की आबादी प्रभावित हुई है। 44 हजार लोग घर छोड़ चुके हैं। राज्य की प्रमुख नदियां भी उफान पर हैं।
यूपी में आज सुबह से ज्यादातर जिलों में धूप निकली है। मौसम विभाग ने आज किसी भी जिले में बारिश का अलर्ट जारी नहीं किया है। राज्य में नदियां अब भी उफान पर हैं। गंगा, शारदा समेत 15 नदियां खतरे के निशान के करीब बह रही हैं। उन्नाव में सई नदी का पानी 12 से ज्यादा गांवों में घुस गया है।
मध्य प्रदेश से शनिवार को मानसून पूरी तरह विदा हो गया। इस बार मानसून पिछले साल के मुकाबले करीब 10 दिन पहले लौटा। यह 24 जून को आया था।
सैटेलाइट मैप में देखें मानसूनी बादलों की स्थिति
देशभर से मौसम की तस्वीरें
राज्यों से मौसम की खबरें…
राजस्थान: अक्टूबर में भी पारा 40 डिग्री के ऊपर, रात में ठंडक
राजस्थान में अक्टूबर में भी दिन के समय तेज गर्मी है। पारा 40 डिग्री के ऊपर पहुंच गया है। सबसे ज्यादा असर पश्चिमी जिलों में है। शुक्रवार को सबसे अधिक तापमान पिलानी (झुंझुनूं) में दर्ज हुआ। पूरी खबर पढ़ें…
यूपी: गोंडा में 25 हजार लोग बाढ़ में फंसे, उन्नाव के 12 गांवों में पानी
यूपी में आज यानी शनिवार सुबह से ज्यादातर जिलों में धूप निकली है। मौसम विभाग ने आज किसी भी जिले में बारिश का अलर्ट जारी नहीं किया है। हालांकि बारिश तो थम गई है, लेकिन नदियां अब भी उफान पर हैं। पूरी खबर पढ़ें…
बिहार: 6 जिलों के 255 गांव पानी में डूबे, 4 लाख आबादी बाढ़ से प्रभावित
बिहार में बाढ़ की स्थिति गंभीर होती जा रही है। गंडक नदी में उफान और तटबंध टूटने से सारण समेत 6 जिलों के करीब 255 गांव बाढ़ की चपेट में हैं। इससे करीब 4 लाख की आबादी प्रभावित हुई है। 44 हजार लोग घर छोड़ चुके हैं। पूरी खबर पढ़ें…
मध्य प्रदेश: राज्य के आधे हिस्से में सूखे जैसे हालात, 25 जिलों में ही सामान्य बारिश
मध्य प्रदेश के आधे हिस्से में सूखे जैसे हालात हैं। 55 में से 30 जिलों में सामान्य बारिश का कोटा पूरा नहीं हुआ है। इनमें भी 11 जिले ऐसे हैं, जहां 80% से कम पानी गिरा। आलीराजपुर में तो आधी बारिश भी नहीं हुई। पूरी खबर पढ़ें…
हरियाणा: अक्टूबर महीने में भी गर्मी बरकरार, महेंद्रगढ़ सबसे गर्म
हरियाणा में अक्टूबर शुरू होने के बावजूद गर्मी से राहत नहीं मिली है। बारिश नहीं होने और मौसम शुष्क रहने से प्रदेश में दिन का तापमान बढ़ रहा है। शुक्रवार को प्रदेश के औसत अधिकतम तापमान में गुरुवार के मुकाबले 0.6 डिग्री सेल्सियस की बढ़ोतरी हुई। पूरी खबर पढ़ें…
पंजाब-चंडीगढ़: ड्राई रहेगा मौसम, बारिश के आसार नहीं
पंजाब और चंडीगढ़ में मौसम अब लगातार ड्राई बना हुआ है। उत्तर-पश्चिमी हवाओं के असर से वातावरण में नमी कम हो रही है और बारिश के आसार भी कम बने हुए हैं। राज्य के औसत अधिकतम तापमान में 0.4 डिग्री की बढ़ोतरी हुई है। पूरी खबर पढ़ें…
हिमाचल: आज से मानसून की विदाई के आसार, छह से आठ तक तेज बारिश
हिमाचल प्रदेश से लगभग सवा तीन महीने बाद आज से मानसून की विदाई के आसार है। अगले 48 घंटे के भीतर पूरे प्रदेश से मानसून विदा हो सकता है। मौसम विज्ञान केंद्र शिमला के अनुसार अभी मानसून की वापसी के लिए परिस्थितियां अनुकूल बनी हुई हैं। पूरी खबर पढ़ें…
उत्तराखंड: आज विदा होगा मानसून, 3-4 अक्टूबर को सभी जिलों में मौसम साफ
उत्तराखंड से आज विदा मानसून हो जाएगा। अगले 24 घंटे में मानसून के प्रदेश के अधिकांश हिस्सों से लौटने की संभावना है। मौसम विभाग के अनुसार, 3 और 4 अक्टूबर को सभी 13 जिलों में मौसम शुष्क रहेगा। मैदानी इलाकों में सुबह हल्के से मध्यम कोहरे की स्थिति बन सकती है। पूरी खबर पढ़ें…

items.title: तिरुपति की फार्मा कंपनी में बॉयलर फटा, 5 की मौत:10 लोग गंभीर घायल; श्री सिटी में हादसे के बाद रेस्क्यू जारी
items.summary: आंध्र प्रदेश के तिरुपति में श्री सिटी की एक फार्मा कंपनी में बॉयलर फट गया। हादसे में पांच लोगों की मौत हो गई है। वहीं, 10 लोग गंभीर रूप से घायल हुए हैं। घायलों को इलाज के लिए अस्पताल पहुंचाया गया है। धमाकों के कारणों का पता नहीं चल पाया है। पुलिस जांच कर रही है। धमाका इतना तेज था कि बिल्डिंग का हिस्सा मलबे में तब्दील हो गया। सत्यवेडु मंडल में हादसे की सूचना मिलते ही पुलिस और इमरजेंसी सर्विस टीमें मौके पर पहुंची और राहत-बचाव का काम शुरू किया। हादसे से जुड़ी तस्वीरें… अधिकारी ने मृतकों की पहचान जा
items.body_text:
- Hindi News
- National
- Sri City Tirupati Pharma Unit Boiler Blast | Deaths & Injuries Update
तिरुपति की फार्मा कंपनी में बॉयलर फटा, 5 की मौत:10 लोग गंभीर घायल; श्री सिटी में हादसे के बाद रेस्क्यू जारी
- कॉपी लिंक
आंध्र प्रदेश के तिरुपति में श्री सिटी की एक फार्मा कंपनी में बॉयलर फट गया। हादसे में पांच लोगों की मौत हो गई है। वहीं, 10 लोग गंभीर रूप से घायल हुए हैं।
घायलों को इलाज के लिए अस्पताल पहुंचाया गया है। धमाकों के कारणों का पता नहीं चल पाया है। पुलिस जांच कर रही है। धमाका इतना तेज था कि बिल्डिंग का हिस्सा मलबे में तब्दील हो गया।
सत्यवेडु मंडल में हादसे की सूचना मिलते ही पुलिस और इमरजेंसी सर्विस टीमें मौके पर पहुंची और राहत-बचाव का काम शुरू किया।
हादसे से जुड़ी तस्वीरें…
अधिकारी ने मृतकों की पहचान जारी नहीं की
एक अधिकारी के मुताबिक, बॉयलर फटने की सही वजह अभी पता नहीं चली है। अधिकारी यह जांच कर रहे हैं कि हादसा तकनीकी खराबी, सुरक्षा व्यवस्था में चूक, संचालन संबंधी लापरवाही या किसी अन्य कारण से हुआ।
अधिकारियों ने अभी सभी मृतकों की पहचान और हादसे की पूरी जानकारी जारी नहीं की है। बचाव अभियान और घायलों की मेडिकल जांच पूरी होने के बाद मृतकों और घायलों की संख्या की पुष्टि होने की उम्मीद है।
राज्य में यह पिछले एक साल में हुआ एक और बड़ा औद्योगिक हादसा है। इसी साल जून में विशाखापट्टनम स्टील प्लांट में पिघला हुआ स्टील ले जा रहा लैडल टूट गया था। इसके बाद आग में 8 कर्मचारियों की मौत हुई थी।
बॉयलर फटने के संभावित कारण
बॉयलर हादसे के पीछे कई तकनीकी कारण हो सकते हैं। सिर्फ पुराने बॉयलर या प्रेशर गेज को जिम्मेदार नहीं माना जा सकता।
- अत्यधिक दबाव: प्रेशर गेज या सेफ्टी वाल्व खराब होने पर दबाव बढ़ सकता है और बॉयलर फट सकता है।
- पानी का स्तर कम होना: इससे बॉयलर ज्यादा गर्म होकर उसकी धातु कमजोर हो सकती है।
- पुराना या खराब रखरखाव: जंग, दरार और स्केल जमने से बॉयलर की क्षमता प्रभावित हो सकती है।
- मानवीय गलती: गलत वाल्व संचालन, खराब प्रशिक्षण या सुरक्षा नियमों का पालन न करना भी हादसे की वजह बन सकता है।

items.title: Men's hockey team retain Asian Games gold to complete historic sweep
items.summary: Mens hockey team retain Asian Games gold to complete historic sweep
items.body_text:
Golden double for India: Men retain hockey gold, completes historic Asian Games sweep
India retained the Asian Games men's hockey gold with a 5-1 win over Malaysia, securing back-to-back titles. The victory completed a historic hockey double after the women's triumph and earned India direct qualification for the LA 2028 Olympics.
India had already celebrated one hockey fairytale. On Saturday, they completed another as the men’s team beat Malaysia 5-1 to retain their Asian Games hockey crown and complete a historic golden double for Indian hockey.
A day after the women’s team ended a 44-year wait for Asian Games gold, the men stepped onto the field with an opportunity to create something just as special. They delivered in emphatic fashion, adding another chapter to a memorable week for Indian hockey.
For the first time, both Indian hockey teams had won gold at the same Asian Games.
India at Asian Games on October 3: Updates | Medal Tally
INDIA START WITH PURPOSE
The men's final began with India playing like a team determined to make the occasion count. They pushed forward from the opening whistle, spending long periods in Malaysian territory and forcing the defence to work. The pressure eventually told when captain Harmanpreet Singh converted a penalty corner in the 11th minute.
Malaysia responded three minutes later through Shelly Silverius, but the equaliser did little to unsettle the defending champions. India went straight back on the attack, probing the Malaysian defence and creating opportunities around the circle.
In the 23rd minute, another penalty corner presented an opportunity and Jugraj Singh made it count. India were back in front and had restored control of the final.
THE GOLD STARTS TO COME INTO VIEW
At half-time, India led 2-1. Malaysia remained within touching distance, but India had established control of the contest and were beginning to dictate the tempo.
The second half brought another gear. In the 42nd minute, vice-captain Hardik Singh converted a penalty stroke to put India 3-1 ahead. Malaysia now had to chase the game, leaving more space for India to exploit.
That space was punished in the 54th minute when Shilanand Lakra completed a flowing attacking move to make it 4-1. Harmanpreet then had the final say in the 57th minute, converting another penalty corner to complete India's five-goal haul.
The final whistle confirmed another Asian Games gold for India.
A MOMENT TO CELEBRATE
When the celebrations began, they belonged to more than just the players on the field. They belonged to an Indian hockey community that had watched the women create history the previous evening and now saw the men successfully defend their own crown.
The women had broken their long wait on Friday, beating reigning champions China 1-0. Twenty-four hours later, the men followed them onto the top step of the podium by beating Malaysia.
Together, they created India's first Asian Games hockey double.
The achievement gave the men's victory an added layer of significance. This was not simply about retaining a title. It was about two teams, separated by a day but united by the same ambition, bringing home gold at the same Games.
ANOTHER CHAPTER FOR INDIAN HOCKEY
The men's triumph also added another golden page to India's Asian Games history. The title is India's fifth men's hockey gold at the Games, following victories in 1966, 1998, 2014 and 2022.
More importantly, India have now successfully defended the men's Asian Games hockey title for the first time. The 2022 triumph in Hangzhou has been followed by another gold in 2026, turning a return to the top into a sustained presence at the summit.
Malaysia took silver, while Pakistan won bronze after defeating South Korea earlier in the day.

items.title: Highest degrees of courage: Dubai crown prince meets hero flydubai pilot
items.summary: Highest degrees of courage Dubai crown prince meets hero flydubai pilot
items.body_text:
Highest degrees of courage: Dubai crown prince meets hero flydubai pilot Smit Machchar
Machchhar is recovering after his Omani co-pilot attacked him with a crash axe aboard the Dubai-Tel Aviv flight on Wednesday. He was shifted to Abu Dhabi after receiving initial treatment in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, where the aircraft made an emergency landing.
UAE Deputy Prime Minister Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed Al Maktoum on Saturday visited Indian flydubai pilot Smit Machchhar in Abu Dhabi, praising his courage in saving passengers during a cockpit attack by his co-pilot.
In a post on X after the visit, Hamdan said Machchhar had shown “the highest degrees of courage, responsibility, and care for human life” and conveyed the UAE leadership’s appreciation.
“We are proud that he is part of our team, part of the story of our nation, and part of what the UAE stands for: A nation of compassion, a nation of peace, and a nation of life,” Dubai's Crown Prince wrote.
Machchhar is recovering in Abu Dhabi after his Omani co-pilot attacked him with a crash axe on Wednesday’s Dubai-Tel Aviv flight, an incident the UAE has called a terrorist attack.
ATTACK ABOARD DUBAI-TEL AVIV FLIGHT
According to the UAE Attorney General's office, the Omani co-pilot attacked Machchhar with a crash axe before trying to take control of flight FZ1073, which carried 174 passengers.
Despite his injuries, Machchhar opened the cockpit door and called for help. Passengers and crew overpowered the attacker, and a reserve crew landed the aircraft at Tabuk airport.
The plane plunged more than 14,000 feet in less than 30 seconds over Saudi Arabia, according to Flightradar24.
Saudi authorities handed the co-pilot over to the UAE after a preliminary investigation involving security teams from both countries.
CO-PILOT’S PAST UNDER SCRUTINY
Al Arabiya identified the co-pilot as Hamam al-Hammami, an Omani national. Three people familiar with the investigation, including a Gulf diplomat and a Western diplomat, also confirmed his identity to the Associated Press.
AP reported that Oman had previously barred al-Hammami from flying over concerns that he had adopted extremist views. He was later hired by flydubai.
It remains unclear what information the airline had about his earlier removal from flying duties or how extensively he was vetted before being hired.
PM MODI SPEAKS TO MACHCHHAR
PM Narendra Modi spoke to Machchhar by video call on Friday, praising his quick thinking during the attack and wishing him a speedy recovery.
“You have taken so many decisions in a fraction of a second. And you have saved the lives of so many people,” he told the pilot.
PM Modi said the entire country was proud of Machchhar. “We Indians are not the ones who take lives. We are the ones who save lives,” he said.
An emotional Machchhar called PM Modi his biggest idol and said he had never imagined getting an opportunity to speak to him. He also said he recited the Hanuman Chalisa during the attack, as he does whenever he faces difficulties.

items.title: 'No fracture': Suvendu accuses Mamata of faking 2021 Nandigram injury, orders probe
items.summary: West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari says Mamata Banerjee faked her 2021 Nandigram injury and cites a medical report as Bengal prepares a fresh inquiry after October 9.
items.body_text:
Image Credit: ANI. West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari and TMC Chief Mamata Banerjee.
West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari has reopened one of the most bitter episodes of the 2021 Assembly election, accusing former chief minister Mamata Banerjee of faking her Nandigram leg injury. He said a March 2021 medical report found no fracture or dislocation and promised a fresh inquiry after the current bypoll code ends on October 9 in Bengal.
Speaking at Nabanna on Saturday, CM Adhikari displayed what he described as a March 11, 2021, report from the Bangur Institute of Neurosciences and said it recorded "no evidence of fracture or dislocation." He said the CID would examine the episode after the Model Code of Conduct is lifted following the Nandigram and Rejinagar bypolls.
"Mamata Banerjee faked her leg injury during campaigning in Nandigram in 2021. We have the medical report which stated that there was no evidence of fracture or dislocation. We will initiate an investigation into the matter," CM Adhikari said.
He added, "Her false allegation insulted the people of Nandigram. I will come out with more details after the MCC is lifted after October 9… Today, I am saying this in support of my claims made yesterday."
#WATCH | Speaking on former CM Mamata Banerjee's injury during the Nandigaram election campaign in 2021, West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari says, "In March 2021, Bangur Institute of Neurosciences shared a report stating that 'there was no evidence of dislocation'. The CID is… pic.twitter.com/HIAtPqUoaA
— ANI (@ANI) October 3, 2026
Former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee was injured on March 10, 2021, while campaigning in Birulia after filing her nomination from Nandigram. She initially said four or five people had pushed her against the open door of her vehicle. In a later hospital video, she said a crowd had pressed towards the car while she was greeting supporters.
Doctors at Kolkata’s SSKM Hospital said at the time that Mamata Banerjee had severe bony injuries to her left ankle and foot, along with injuries and pain involving her shoulder, forearm and neck. She was discharged on March 12 after treatment and later campaigned in a wheelchair.
The report cited by CM Adhikari now concerns the absence of a fracture or dislocation. Contemporary hospital statements recorded injuries, so the fresh inquiry will examine whether Mamata Banerjee's public account of the 2021 injury matched the medical material and other records from the case.
The Election Commission examined the incident during the 2021 campaign. Its observers, Ajay Nayak and Vivek Dube, found no evidence of a premeditated or planned attack and said the incident appeared to have happened accidentally. The Commission later acted against officials over security lapses, including Mamata Banerjee's security director and district officials.
The CID also took over the original 2021 case, which had been registered after a complaint by Trinamool Congress leader Sheikh Sufiyan. The case was based on Mamata Banerjee's allegation that she had been deliberately targeted.
CM Adhikari said no further step would be announced until the bypoll process ends. Nandigram votes on October 6, and the result is due on October 9.

items.title: Opinion | How Yogi Adityanath turned Uttar Pradesh's expressways from single road into state network
items.summary: Nine named corridors with a published official cost are already open. Their combined project outlay is ₹124,777.94 crore, treated as utilised because the assets are commissioned.
items.body_text:
Image Credit: ANI. Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath.
Dr Patanjali Mishra
A state the size of Uttar Pradesh cannot be governed from one city and visited from the others. Distance has long been its hidden tax: on the price of a sack of grain, on the hour a patient spends between districts, on whether a factory in Jhansi or Ghazipur is a site or a rumour. Since 2017 the Yogi Adityanath government has treated that distance as an engineering problem. The result, on figures compiled from UPEIDA, MoRTH and Cabinet papers as of 30 August 2026, is no longer a single road. It is a grid.
Nine named corridors with a published official cost are already open. Their combined project outlay is ₹124,777.94 crore, treated as utilised because the assets are commissioned. Purvanchal, 340.8 kilometers, was tendered afresh in 2018, foundation-stoned that July and opened on 16 November 2021 at ₹22,494.66 crore including land. Bundelkhand, 296 kilometers, opened on 16 July 2022 at ₹14,850 crore. The Gorakhpur Link, 91.4 kilometers, opened on 20 June 2025 at ₹7,283.28 crore. The Ganga Expressway, about 594 kilometers from Meerut to Prayagraj, was taken to Cabinet at ₹36,230 crore and opened on 29 April 2026. The Lucknow–Kanpur expressway, reported after opening at ₹4,200 crore, opened on 13 July 2026. Around them sit the Eastern Peripheral Expressway, inaugurated in May 2018 at a MoRTH construction cost of ₹4,417.89 crore, and the Delhi–Meerut Expressway, fully open from 1 April 2021 at ₹7,855.87 crore. These are not ribbons between the same two cities. Purvanchal ties the east to Lucknow. Bundelkhand ties the dry south-west to the same capital. Ganga runs the spine toward Prayagraj. Gorakhpur is no longer a terminus.
Eight further UPEIDA corridors have a published cabinet cost and are not yet open: Chitrakoot, the Lucknow link; Farrukhabad, the Jewar–Ganga link; Jhansi, the Meerut–Haridwar extension; Vindhya from Prayagraj to Sonbhadra; and the Mirzapur–Ghazipur spur. Together they are professed at Rs 75,873.06 crore. Printed 2026-27 releases that can be tied to this new grid – land and token construction – come to Rs 15,390 crore. Add the open stock and the approved stock and the usable published total is Rs 2,00,651 crore, of which Rs 1,40,167.94 crore is known as disbursed or utilised. State highways sit on a different ledger: the Public Works Department spent about Rs 28,087 crore in 2025-26 against an allocation of Rs 32,676 crore. That is ordinary road stock. It is what makes an expressway usable on the last mile.
The economic claim follows the map, not a brochure. A mill, a mandi or a ward is worth more when the truck does not lose a day. Bundelkhand's expressway is the missing argument for industry on a plateau that politics once described only as scarce. Purvanchal shortens the east’s path to the state capital and, through it, to the west. The Jewar link and the Ganga alignment are aimed at an airport and a riverine corridor, not at a ceremonial avenue. Daily use is plainer still. An inter-district transfer, a wedding party, a load of cane: each is a toll receipt and a saved hour. Neighbouring states are already in the drawing. The Eastern Peripheral and Delhi–Meerut roads bind the National Capital Region; the Haridwar extension and the Agra-side national corridors are meant to carry the same standard past the state line.
The contrast with the Samajwadi years is not that nothing was built. The Agra–Lucknow Expressway, 302.22 kilometres, was constructed between 2014 and 2016 and opened in November 2016 at an official cost later stated at Rs14,446 crore. The Yamuna Expressway, opened on 9 August 2012, belongs to a concession signed in 2003. What those years did not leave was a clean ledger or a network. On the Yamuna project, the allegation is that the then YEIDA chief executive, P.C. Gupta, and others bought 57.15 hectares cheaply through nineteen companies and sold it back to the authority at a higher price, a loss put at Rs 126

items.title: 'Power without discipline dangerous': LG Sinha's message to Kashmir youth on AI
items.summary: LG Sinha urged Kashmir youth to embrace AI and modern technology while staying rooted in Mahatma Gandhi's values of truth, morality and compassion.
items.body_text:
Image Credit: ANI. Jammu and Kashmir Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha.
Jammu and Kashmir Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha on Gandhi Jayanti urged Kashmir’s youth to embrace artificial intelligence and modern technology while remaining rooted in Mahatma Gandhi’s principles of truth, non-violence, discipline and compassion. He added that technological power must be guided by morality and human values to benefit society and the nation.
Addressing students and youth in Srinagar on the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti, Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha stressed the need to balance technological progress with ethical values. His remarks focused particularly on the growing influence of artificial intelligence and the responsibility that comes with access to powerful digital tools.
LG Manoj Sinha said, “When I used to study in primary school, I still remember a simple truth of those days. If you went to any village or any small town and asked, ‘Where does the Guru live?’, almost anyone could point the way. The house of the teacher, the spiritual guide, the shaper of character, was known to all. Today, times have changed. Today, almost everyone can tell you where the merchant’s house stands, where commerce flourishes and wealth is counted. But fewer people remain who can still point out the Guru’s house.
He recalled Mahatma Gandhi’s teachings, saying that the character of a nation is its most permanent and fundamental structure and that the moral character of its people ultimately determines the country’s destiny.
“Revered Bapu believed that the character of a nation is its most permanent and fundamental structure. Buildings may rise and fall, markets may boom and slow, but the moral character of a people is what ultimately decides the destiny of a country,” he said.
Sinha also recalled Mahatma Gandhi’s association with Kashmir and his message of peace and brotherhood, saying that Gandhi had seen Kashmir as a symbol of hope for peace and communal harmony during a period of widespread violence and hatred.
“Mahatma Gandhi held Kashmir and its people in the highest respect. At a time when the entire country was burning with the fire of hate and violence, Gandhi visited Kashmir and found brotherhood still intact. It was then that he uttered those immortal words: ‘if there is any ray of hope for peace and love I see that ray of hope from Kashmir,’” he said.
“Those words were not spoken lightly. They reflected the deep faith he placed in the people of this land, a people who had absorbed his message of peace, non-violence and love, and kept that flame alive even in the darkest hours. The Kashmiri people had, in their own quiet way, lived the teachings of Gandhi. That ray of hope which Bapu saw must now be turned into a beacon for the entire nation,” he added.
Sinha said the younger generation has access to technological resources that earlier generations could not have imagined, while urging them to use such tools responsibly.
“You possess resources that we, in our student days, could not even imagine. In your palm rests a mobile phone more powerful than the greatest libraries of earlier centuries. In your hands lies Artificial Intelligence, a force capable of solving complex problems, creating new knowledge, and connecting the world at a speed never known before. You have access to the entire information of humanity, and you possess the unprecedented power to send your voice, your ideas, and your message across the globe in an instant. But power without discipline is dangerous. Knowledge without morality is emptiness. Technology without values is a double-edged sword that can cut both ways,” he said.
Sinha said, “I urge you to use these extraordinary modern technology tools, especially Artificial Intelligence, with the same iron discipline and unwavering morality that revered Mahatma Gandhi practised every single day of his life. items.title: Meet Madan Lokur, ex-SC judge turned ‘activist’ now eyeing to run parallel judiciary with ‘independent commission’ on SIR
items.summary: While Justice Lokur has been critical of the government at home, he has had warm and cordial relations with Pakistani judges. In January 2019, the former apex court judge attended the swearing-in ceremony of the former Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Pakistan, Asif Saeed Khosa, who is also said to be his close friend.
items.body_text:
LAFC announces an Independent Commission of Former Supreme Court & High Court Judges to examine the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
Chaired by Justice Madan B. Lokur, the Commission will undertake public hearings, legal research and scrutiny. pic.twitter.com/p6J0AXpyeC
— Lawyers' Association For Constitution (@lafcindia) October 2, 2026
The Commission has been tasked to conduct an ‘independent inquiry’ to find out if the SIR exercise was undertaken by the Election Commission in a fair manner. The full panel of the commission will be travelling across the country, hearing testimony of citizens allegedly affected by the SIR exercise and collecting data on the additions or deletions in the electoral rolls, as stated in the press release of the LAFC.
Apart from the intriguing composition of the commission, the timing of its formation is also interesting. The commission comes at a time when the Opposition and mainstream media portals like the Indian Express are trying hard to push a narrative to cast aspersions on the Election Commission by alleging irregularities in the SIR exercise and connivance with the BJP government. What adds to the suspicion is that the head of the commission, retired Justice Lokur, is known for being at odds with the current BJP government.
Criticised abrogation of Article 370 and the UAPA law
Justice Lokur had criticised the abrogation of Article 370 by the Modi government, which was upheld by the Supreme Court itself. He also voiced his objections to the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act (UAPA), which empowers the government to effectively deal with anti-national activities.
He was part of the infamous rebel group of four judges who held an unprecedented press conference in 2018, with allegations, including the government’s lack of response to the Memorandum of Procedure (MoP) governing the appointment of judges. Justice Lokur was also on the Constitutional Bench that, in 2015, struck down the National Judicial Appointment Commission (NJAC), introduced by the Modi government to replace the controversial Collegium system for the appointment of judges.
Friends with Pakistani Judges
While Justice Lokur has been critical of the government at home, he has had warm and cordial relations with Pakistani judges. In January 2019, the former apex court judge attended the swearing-in ceremony of the former Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Pakistan, Asif Saeed Khosa, who is also said to be a close friend of his. This was not the only time that the former judge attended the swearing-in ceremony of a judge in Pakistan. Years before this, he had also taken part in the swearing-in ceremony of former Pakistan Chief Justice Tassaduq Hussain Jillani, when he took the oath as the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court.
Member of a foreign-funded NGO, opposed NRC detentions
The former Supreme Court judge is also a senior member of an NGO funded by the US State Department. He is an Executive Committee member of the Commonwealth Human Rights Initiative (CHRI). As a CHRI member, he signed a statement along with other so-called ’eminent citizens’ against the detention of illegal immigrants under the National Register of Citizens (NRC) framework and the setting up of detention centres.
CHRI monitors the ‘human rights situation’ across the Commonwealth through its International Advocacy and Programming (IAP) unit, which explains Justice Lokur’s stance against detentions and detention centres under the NRC framework. Pertinently, the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) suspended the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA) license of the CHRI in June 2021. items.title: ‘Machchhar’ means more than a mosquito: The fascinating story behind Captain Smit Machchhar’s Gujarati surname
items.summary: A surname is more than just a second name; it conveys an untold story of some unknown ancestor. With surnames like 'Mankad' (insect), 'Machchhar' (mosquito), or 'Ghoda' (horse), these untold stories become even more intriguing. This is because the moment such a surname is spoken, one visualizes an insect or an animal rather than a person.
items.body_text:
Some surnames are so unique that they stick in your memory right from the moment you hear them for the first time. One such surname is ‘Machchhar’ (Mosquito). In everyday conversation, the word ‘Machchhar’ conjures up the image of a creature buzzing near one’s ear on a summer night; yet, when the same word appears after a person’s name, one wonders about the origin of such a surname.
Captain Smit Machchhar, with his distinctive surname, is once again in the headlines. He became a global talking point after he valiantly prevented a Jihadi crashing attempt on a Flydubai flight en route from Dubai to Tel Aviv. Despite being brutally stabbed by his Omani co-pilot, Smit Machchhar managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers to bring the aircraft under control. The plane made an emergency landing safely at Tabuk Airport in Saudi Arabia. All 174 passengers on board landed safely, and Smit Machchhar was widely praised for his courage.
Smit Machchhar’s courage attracted global applause. However, apart from his valour, his surname also gained wider attention and made people question: how does a person come to have ‘Machchhar’ as a surname? While such a surname might surprise people around the world, in Gujarat, such surnames are common. In the state, one finds surnames like ‘Mankad’ (Bedbug), ‘Ghoda’ (Horse), ‘Chakli’ (Sparrow), ‘Titodi’ (Lapwing), ‘Popat’ (Parrot), ‘Bakri’ (Goat), ‘Tagh’ (Tiger/Leopard), and ‘Hathi’ (Elephant). These surnames are unique not only because of how interesting they sound but also because their origins are linked to simple but fascinating stories, often about a person’s life, appearance, temperament, village, home, or even a joke.
An old book titled History of Gujarati Surnames (Gujarati Upnamon no Itihas) examines surnames derived from animals, birds, or insects. Such surnames are rare and are more prevalent in the Kathiawad region of Gujarat. No conclusive account can be given regarding the origins of these surnames. There are multiple possibilities, and in many instances, conjecture outweighs concrete evidence. Therefore, it is not possible to provide an accurate account of the origins of such surnames; however, we can glance through all the stories linked to their origins.
Surnames do not always carry a single meaning
We often associate surnames with a specific meaning. For example, ‘Gandhi’ implies a particular Gandhi family, ‘Patel’ signifies a specific lineage, and ‘Desai’ denotes a particular heritage. However, the history of surnames is not so straightforward. A word can be carried by different families as a surname and can acquire a distinct meaning for specific reasons. A surname might originate from a place name, a profession, an ancestor’s name, or an existing epithet; alternatively, a nickname given in jest might evolve into a permanent surname over generations.
This holds for surnames derived from animals or insects. Just because ‘Bagh’ (Tiger) and ‘Hathi’ (Elephant) are both names of animals, it is not enough to assume that the two surnames share a common origin. Similarly, while ‘Mankad’ (Bedbug) and ‘Machchhar’ (Mosquito) might sound like equally peculiar surnames, they could well have originated under entirely different circumstances and be unrelated to one another. The origins of each such surname need to be examined individually. This is where the subject becomes intriguing; the question is no longer merely about how the name ‘Machchhar’ came to be. Instead, the question becomes: how did people in the Gujarat of the past assign such surnames to identify individuals within their society?
Sometimes surnames originate from unique nicknames.
In the old times, a person’s official name could be different from the name by which the local community knew him. items.title: Trump Says US and Canada Have Reached Last-Minute Deal to Delay 50% US Tariffs on Canadian Imports
items.summary: The announcement, which Trump made on his social media platform, buys time for more negotiations and avoids, for now, another strain in already tense relations between the historic allies.
items.body_text:
Trump Says US and Canada Have Reached Last-Minute Deal to Delay 50% US Tariffs on Canadian Imports
The announcement, which Trump made on his social media platform, buys time for more negotiations and avoids, for now, another strain in already tense relations between the historic allies.
- World News
- 4 min read
Washington: President Donald Trump said Tuesday he was delaying 50% U.S. tariffs on $20 billion worth of Canadian imports after the two countries reached a last-minute deal hours before the sanctions were to go into effect.
The announcement, which Trump made on his social media platform, buys time for more negotiations and avoids, for now, another strain in already tense relations between the historic allies.
“I have paused the 50% Tariffs against Canada, that were scheduled to kick in tomorrow morning for three days, based on the fact that Canada and the U.S.A., subject to the finalisation of documents, have a DEAL!” Trump posted on Truth Social less than two hours before the 12:01 a.m. Wednesday deadline.
If they had gone into effect as scheduled at 12:01 a.m. Wednesday, Trump’s import taxes would have hit Canadian products ranging from hockey sticks to tongue depressors.
Advertisement
But the political impact would likely have been bigger than the economic one. Canada had threatened to retaliate against any new tariffs with levies of its own, aggravating a trade fight between countries that sold each other $880 billion worth of goods and services last year.
Canadian officials did not immediately respond to requests for comment Tuesday night.
Advertisement
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Trump had spoken twice by phone in the past two days about the ongoing negotiations, including a call Tuesday afternoon, Carney’s office said, underscoring the last-minute push for a deal.
Both countries had reason to step back from the brink. Nearly 72% of Canada’s goods exports last year went to the United States. And the Trump administration would be taking a risk by imposing a hefty new tariff — paid by U.S. importers who try to pass along the cost to consumers via higher prices — ahead of November’s midterm elections. U.S. voters are already frustrated with the high cost of living.
“I don’t think either side really wants these tariffs to come into effect,’’ Ryan Majerus, a partner at King & Spalding and a former U.S. trade official, said before the delay was announced. “There’s a pretty strong push on both sides to find an off-ramp here.’’
Trump’s approach to dealing with Canada marks an extraordinary departure from the traditionally cooperative relationship between the two countries. Trump has hit Canadian goods with tariffs — in a push to bring manufacturing back to the U.S. — and has repeatedly made inflammatory comments about turning Canada into America’s 51st state.
Trump has made tariffs the centrepiece of his second-term economic agenda. Last year, he imposed double-digit import taxes on almost every country, justifying them by declaring the longstanding U.S. trade deficit a national emergency. The Supreme Court in February ruled that he’d overstepped his authority, striking down those tariffs and setting the stage for the federal government to pay refunds to importers.
So Trump has looked for other legal authority to impose tariffs.
To hit Canada, he reached back to the Great Depression, invoking Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 to threaten 50% tariffs on products that account for about 5% of Canadian exports to the United States.
Nearly a century ago, with the U.S. and world economies in collapse, Congress passed the 1930 tariff law, imposing taxes on imports from around the world. Known as the Smoot-Hawley tariffs, named for their congressional sponsors, they are notorious among economists and historians for limiting world commerce and making the Great Depression worse.
Section 338 tariffs have never been used before.
Section 338 authorises the president to impose tariffs of up to 50% on imports from count

items.body_text:
'Allegations Lack Seriousness': Turkiye Denies Israel's Claims Over Syria Airstrikes
"These air strikes should stop, and we stand against them," Dujarric said at a UN press briefing on Tuesday. As per Al Jazeera, Egypt's Foreign Ministry also condemned the Israeli strikes, calling them a "dangerous escalation that threatens security and stability in the region".
- World News
- 3 min read
Ankara: Turkiye on Wednesday rejected Israel's claim that its airstrikes on Syria's Abu al-Duhur military airport were linked to a planned Turkish troop deployment, saying the allegations "lack seriousness" and seek to legitimise strikes on Syria's sovereignty and territorial integrity.
In a post on X, the Turkish Presidential Communications Directorate said, “The allegations put forward by the Israeli Prime Ministry, which lack seriousness, aim to legitimize Israel's unlawful airstrikes targeting the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Syria.” It added, "The accusations raised stem from Netanyahu's intent to continue his expansionist and destabilizing policies in the region ahead of elections in Israel."
Turkiye said it supports the establishment of lasting peace in the region, adding that "the sole path to this lies in Netanyahu abandoning his aggressive and coercive policies and demonstrating respect for international law". "Turkey will steadfastly continue its cooperation with the Syrian Government on legitimate grounds to establish peace, stability, and prosperity in Syria, and will never allow Syria to be destabilized," it said.
The remarks came after Israel carried out airstrikes on the Abu al-Duhur military airport in Syria's eastern Idlib province. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office said that Syria was allowing Turkish troops to deploy at an airbase near Aleppo. Meanwhile, on Tuesday (local time), UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres' spokesperson Stephane Dujarric called the strikes "yet another very worrying violation" of Syria's territorial integrity and airspace.
Advertisement
"These air strikes should stop, and we stand against them," Dujarric said at a UN press briefing on Tuesday. As per Al Jazeera, Egypt's Foreign Ministry also condemned the Israeli strikes, calling them a "dangerous escalation that threatens security and stability in the region".
In a statement, the ministry said Egypt "fully rejects" Israel's continued violations of Syrian sovereignty and warned that the strikes could further destabilise Syria at a critical time when the country requires support to restore stability and pursue political solutions. Cairo called on the international community to "assume its responsibilities" by putting an end to repeated Israeli violations and adopting firm measures to deter actions that could fuel a broader regional conflict.
Advertisement
Earlier on Tuesday, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office said Israel and Syria had agreed to maintain a security "status quo". In a post on X, Netanyahu's office said, "Israel and Syria agreed to a status quo in security matters, which Syria was on the verge of breaching by permitting Turkish troops to deploy at an airbase near Aleppo," the statement said.
"Israel will not tolerate threats to its security, and would welcome a return to the status quo," it added. Meanwhile, US Special Presidential Envoy for Syria and Iraq Tom Barrack expressed concern over the Israeli airstrikes, calling them an "unnecessary escalation". "We are deeply concerned that the confirmed Israeli airstrikes on Abu al-Duhur Airbase constitute an unnecessary escalation that does not advance regional stability," Barrack said.
The airbase was targeted in four airstrikes, marking the first reported attack on the facility since the fall of former Syrian President Bashar al-Assad's government in December 2024.

Ottawa: With Ottawa and Washington continually engaged in discussions over the 50 per cent tariff on a select range of Canadian goods, Prime Minister Mark Carney said that the implementation of the tariffs has been postponed until August 21.
Sharing the remarks in a letter posted on X, Prime Minister Carney reassured that while rigorous engagements remain in place with Washington, Canada remains focused on building a stronger, more independent, and more competitive economy at home.
"Over the last number of weeks, Canada has engaged in intensive discussions with the United States to address outstanding trade issues and deliver greater certainty and real benefits for Canadian businesses, workers, farmers and families," he said.
The Canadian Prime Minister observed that while significant headway has been made, key work remains to be done. Substantial progress has been made, although there is important work still to be done. As this work is ongoing, the United States has agreed to postpone the implementation of its 50% tariff on a range of Canadian goods under Section 338 of the U.S. Tariff Act of 1930 until the end of day, August 21," he said.

The announcement comes in the nick of time as the Trump administration's latest round of tariffs was originally scheduled to take effect at 12:01 a.m. Eastern Time on Wednesday.
According to Canadian public broadcaster CBC, the levies would have applied to hundreds of products worth more than USD 28 billion, from plywood and cement to wine and hockey sticks.

items.title: Asian Games: Gold Again! India Thrash Malaysia 5-1 To Defend Men’s Hockey Title
items.summary: Asian Games: Gold Again! India Thrash Malaysia 5-1 To Defend Men’s Hockey Title
items.body_text:
Asian Games Hockey Final: India produced a commanding display in the Asian Games 2026 men’s hockey final, defeating Malaysia 5-1 at the Gifu Prefectural Green Stadium in Kakamigahara, Japan, to successfully retain their gold medal. The final began cautiously, with both sides refusing to commit too many players overwhelmingly forward. India eventually broke the deadlock through their captain Harmanpreet Singh, who converted a penalty corner to put his side in front. Malaysia responded soon after, ensuring India did not have things all their own way. Jugraj & Hardik Put India In Control India regained the advantage in the second quarter when Jugraj Singh found the net from another penalty corner. The goal gave India a 2-1 cushion at the interval and provided them with a platform to build on. The Indian defence remained disciplined after the break, but there was little room for complacency. Read More: India vs Brazil Live Streaming: When & Where To Watch India had surrendered a three-goal advantage against Pakistan in the semi-final before eventually winning, making concentration crucial in the gold-medal clash. Hardik Singh then extended India’s advantage in the third quarter, converting a penalty stroke to make it 3-1. The two-goal lead gave India greater breathing room heading into the final period. Late Goals Seal Another Asian Games Gold Malaysia continued to search for a way back into the contest, but India remained composed at the back while looking dangerous going forward. With just over six minutes remaining, Shilanand Lakra effectively put the result beyond doubt by scoring India’s fourth goal, from open play. The final blow came soon after, with Harmanpreet adding another to his tally after India were awarded a penalty corner following a referral. The 5-1 victory completed a successful title defence for India and capped a dominant gold-medal performance. After navigating a challenging route to the final, India delivered when it mattered most to retain their Asian Games crown.

The final match took place at the Gifu Prefectural Green Stadium in Kakamigahara, Japan.
