items.title: Inside Germany: Why I travelled half way around the world to be married
items.summary: Whether it's just over the border in Denmark or the other side of the world in your home country, for non-Germans getting married is often easier literally anywhere but Germany, writes The Local editor Paul Krantz.
items.body_text:
This week I’m freshly back at my desk after a couple weeks off during which I flew around 8,500 kilometres to be wed.
The decision to fly across eight time zones for a wedding may sound like an overindulgent choice. In fact when my (now) wife and I initially discussed our plans, we agreed we wanted to avoid the headache and the cost of anything too big and complicated.
But, my beat being the challenges of living in Germany as a foreigner, I knew before we even began that getting married in this country was basically a dead-end for us.
So – for all the other internationals in Germany who are thinking about tying the knot – here’s why it was easier for me to fly halfway around the world than get married at my local registry office.
What it takes for foreigners to get married in Germany
A couple of years ago I interviewed a Canadian national about the process he navigated to be married to his French wife in Berlin.
In the end the couple did marry successfully, but the process involved months of gathering documents and translations, and spamming every registry office (Standesamt) in Berlin for an appointment.
It was described to me as “the final boss” of German bureaucracy.
READ ALSO: 'Clunky process' - The steps you need to take to get married in Germany
Language skills
The first barrier to getting married in Germany for many foreigners is the language requirement. All official civil weddings in Germany are conducted in German.
Navigating all of the proceedings, speech, questions and paperwork requires a pretty solid command of the language.
I’m not shy to admit that my own German is less than perfect and my wife's is even more of a work in progress. So had we tried to go through with the German ceremony, we would have needed to hire an official interpreter (Dolmetscher) to attend, and translate for us.
It’s worth noting that if you have a witness at your wedding in Germany, which is optional, they too are on the hook for understanding everything that’s being said.
A funny detail in the story linked above was that the wedding itself was nearly derailed when the groom’s witness asked a simple clarifying question in English. The officiant suddenly turned quite serious, and said they would have to end the ceremony if the witness couldn't respond in German (because this would show they had not understood the proceedings).
Papers and translations
The next hurdle, in typically German bureaucratic fashion, is gathering all the paperwork, and – for most foreigners – also official translations. In most cases these include:
- Birth certificates
- Valid passports or IDs
- A registration certificate for your current address (Erweiterte Meldebescheinigung), which is not more than 14 days old.
- A certificate of no impediment to marriage (Ehefähigkeitszeugnis), or an exemption if your country does not issue them.
Collecting each of these documents is usually easy enough, but getting each of them and their translations all within a tight time window is the trick.
The person I spoke to described needing to request a birth certificate from Canada, waiting for it in the mail, and then sending it back to the same authority to have the translation notarised.
Luck with getting an appointment
Finally, if you manage to clear all the preliminary hurdles, the final challenge can be getting an appointment to be married.
A tricky bottleneck here is that you first need an appointment to file your intent to marry (Anmeldung der Eheschließung) where you turn in the paperwork. Then you have a six month window during which the ceremony can take place.
Getting an appointment for a ceremony in that time is not always easy, depending on where in Germany you live – and especially if you're aiming for a particular location like Berlin's Rotes Rathaus, for example.

items.title: Does Germany really have the most punishing tax system for foreigners?
items.summary: Germany sits dead last in a recent ranking of countries by 'tax optimisation for global citizens', but it's also near the top of the list for quality of life.
items.body_text:
A recent global ranking of countries' tax codes attempts to answer the question, 'Where do foreign residents face the least tax burden?'
Among the 48 countries compared, Germany ranked dead last – meaning that foreigners living here face a higher tax burden than they would in any of the other locations.
So why does Germany rank so poorly for tax optimisation for foreign residents, and how does that affect quality of life for those who pay their dues to the Bundesrepublik?
The ranking, published this month by Global Citizen Solutions (GCS), compared 48 jurisdictions around the world to find those with the best tax optimisation for foreign residents.
The GCS report defines tax optimisation as "the arrangement of one’s affairs, within the law, so as to minimize the tax legally due..."
It adds that in a globalised world, many people can now choose where they want to relocate, and that certain tax regimes are intentionally written to attract high earners.
Germany as a high-burden system
The index was based on 11 indicators that were sorted into three categories; tax burden (including personal income tax, capital gains tax, wealth and inheritance tax), tax structure (including how systems treated internationally sourced income, exit taxes and VAT), and investment migration (which looked at opportunities to invest in a country in exchange for gaining residency or citizenship rights).
Jurisdictions received a score in each category, as well as a composite score meant to represent its overall tax burden for foreigners.
Germany's composite score was the lowest of all the countries analysed, meaning that it was evaluated to have the highest tax burden for foreigners.
Of the categories listed above, Germany's lowest score was in the 'tax structure', which covers the treatment of foreign income and also taxes related to leaving the country.
Notably residents of Germany are taxed on their total global income, including income earned overseas as long as they maintain German residency.
READ ALSO: How closely will Germany's Finanzamt look at your tax return?
As for so-called exit taxes, these primarily affect investors or business owners who have been long-term residents in Germany.
Germany's exit tax (Wegzugsbesteuerung) applies to anyone who has been a tax resident of the country for at least seven of the last 12 years, and owns at least one percent of a corporation. A person in this position who moves abroad is taxed on the sale price of those corporate shares, even if they have not sold the shares.
While Germany's tax structure was rated worst for foreigners, its score in the 'tax burden' category – which dealt with income, inheritance and wealth taxes – was not at the bottom. Spain, France and Denmark all had higher burdens for foreigners than Germany, according to the ranking.
Regarding inheritance taxes in Germany, one key note for foreign residents is that they do apply to inheritance coming from overseas.
How does tax optimisation affect quality of life?
Germany's position at the bottom of the GCS's tax optimisation ranking implies that foreigners who move here can expect to pay more in taxes than those who move elsewhere – especially compared to say the UAE, Hong Kong or Malta, which ranked near the top of the list.
But how does that affect quality of life for those who do decide to move to Germany? The answer seems to be that when comparing life quality between countries, generally, you get what you pay for.
When countries' tax optimisation scores were compared against their 'quality of life' rankings from the Global Passport Index 2026, the overall trend was that countries offering the highest quality of life tended to offer lower tax optimisation.
Sweden had the second highest quality of life ranking, but was 32nd out of 48 in GCS's tax ranking. Germany was 3rd in the world for quality of life, but last for tax optimisation.

items.title: How long are EES waiting times at German airports?
items.summary: With the autumn break coming up, many people may be wondering what kind of delays to expect at German airports due to the Entry and Exit System (EES) checks.
items.body_text:
October is prime time for travel in and out of Germany, with schools in many states off for the Herbstferien – and residents looking for an extra dose of sunshine before winter sets in.
However, travellers passing through Germany's airports may face longer waits at border control following the introduction of the EU's Entry/Exit System (EES).
A reader recently got in touch with The Local to flag up increased waiting times at Frankfurt and Munich airports.
So what is the situation currently – and what can we expect in the coming weeks?
What's happening at Frankfurt Airport?
Germany's largest airport – Frankfurt – hit the headlines recently after travellers reported long waiting times at the border.
According to German media, the delays were due to "technical problems" with the entry and exit computer system.
The new biometric border check scheme involves logging more information from travellers, including fingerprints and facial scans. The EES has been recording each entry and exit to the Schengen area of non-EU short-term visitors since it was gradually introduced in October 2025.
READ ALSO: How EES border checks affect EasyPASS users travelling to and from Germany
Once a traveller's biometric data has been registered, it is stored in the system for three years, meaning that they should not have to repeat the full registration process each time they cross the external Schengen border during that period.
The situation at Frankfurt has since eased but airport operators Fraport have urged travellers to factor in long queues due to the busy season.
Between October 2nd and 18th, Frankfurt airport is expecting around 3.5 million passengers. In the first autumn break weekend (October 2nd-4th) alone, an estimated 650,000 people will fly through Frankfurt.
In a press statement, the airport said that due to the increased passenger numbers, travellers from non-EU countries in particular could see even longer waits.
"The EES improves European security as well as border protection and Fraport supports its implementation, including providing additional personnel," said a Fraport spokesperson.
"Nevertheless, the EES requirements for entering and leaving the EU are resulting in longer wait times at border checks, especially for non-EU citizens.
"This is why we are advising passengers from non-EU countries, in particular, to allow adequate time for the necessary procedures and to arrive at the airport at least three hours before their departure time."
What about German residents?
People who live in Germany on a valid residence permit – including non-EU residents – as well as EU and Schengen citizens, should not face the same EES registration process as non-EU short-term visitors.
However, Frankfurt airport warned that these groups "could also experience longer wait times" at the border "as a result of these new regulations and, if they are traveling to countries outside of the Schengen Area, should arrive at the airport three hours prior to departure".
The airport added that these passengers are allowed to use the EasyPASS automated border control system, which reduces wait times at the borders.
Passengers who do not have to pass through border control are advised to arrive at the airport around two and a half hours before their departure time.
For those travelling only with hand luggage, they should arrive about two hours before their flight is due to leave.
What's happening at other airports?
In general, airports across Europe say that EES has increased waiting times.
According to a report from travel analytics group Qsensor which was reported on by the Financial Times, the average 'maximum queue time' at Munich airport rose from 31 minutes in 2025 to 60 minutes in July 2026.
At Frankfurt, average maximum wait times reached 120 minutes, double the 60 minutes recorded in July 2025.

items.title: Tokayev: AI should complement, not replace human intelligence
items.summary: President of Kazakhstan Kassym-Jomart Tokayev emphasized that artificial intelligence should not be viewed as a ...
items.body_text:
“There is no doubt that alongside huge opportunities, we will have to face many shakeups and even upheavals. Therefore, we must develop AI with full responsibility and integrity,” Tokayev said in a statement from the Embassy of Kazakhstan in Jakarta on Saturday.
He made the remarks during the opening of the AI & Digital Bridge 2026 international technology forum, which is being held in Astana from October 1 to 3.
According to Tokayev, as technology advances at an ever-faster pace, critical thinking, the pursuit of knowledge, and individual responsibility are becoming increasingly important.
He said regulatory requirements should be stringent only where security and the vital interests of citizens are at stake, so as to ensure that promising talent and investment remain in the country.
Tokayev proposed identifying real-world demand for AI solutions across the economy and launching an AI Challenge initiative, with the most promising solutions subsequently deployed in industry.
He also underscored the need for the highest degree of responsibility and integrity in the development of artificial intelligence.
In that context, he welcomed President Donald Trump’s initiative under which leading U.S. technology companies signed an accord setting out safety principles for the development of advanced AI systems.
“From my perspective, this approach could be regarded by all countries involved as a model to be adopted globally after serious consideration,” Tokayev said.
Tokayev also said that the accord could also serve as a reference point in shaping approaches to AI governance during the third meeting of the Council for the Development of Artificial Intelligence.
“The accord signed in Washington D.C. could be regarded by all countries involved as a model to be introduced worldwide in the AI sector to be eventually passed after serious consideration by experts,” Tokayev said.
“And this ‘Washington Model’ may become a core of an International Treaty under the auspices of the UN,” he added.
Kazakhstan is ready to facilitate substantive international dialogue on the issues, Tokayev said, urging Council members to submit concrete proposals on Kazakhstan’s initiative. He said their shared vision would be presented at the G20 Summit in Miami this December.
Kazakhstan is holding “AI Month” from September 23 to October 23 as part of the Year of Digitalization and Artificial Intelligence.
The Council for the Development of Artificial Intelligence and the AI & Digital Bridge 2026 international technology forum are the main events of “AI Month”.
The month-long program features a wide range of events dedicated to artificial intelligence and digital technologies, bringing together the technology community, businesses, educational institutions, startups, international experts, and regional initiatives from across the country.

items.title: Ministry promotes low-carbon aquaculture to boost exports
items.summary: The Indonesian Ministry of National Development Planning is encouraging the adoption of low-carbon aquaculture to open ...
items.body_text:
The ministry's Deputy for Food, Natural Resources, and Environmental Affairs, Leonardo Adypurnama, said in North Sumatra on Friday that global demand for seafood traceability is on the rise.
This is because market traceability now extends beyond simply knowing where a product originates, it also requires verifying that production methods are sustainable.
Speaking during a visit to floating net cages operated by PT Suri Tani Pemuka (Japfa) in Lake Toba, he stated that the initiative is fundamentally part of Indonesia's broader commitment to low-carbon development.
According to him, Indonesia was previously the world's second-largest tilapia producer and exporter, but was overtaken by Vietnam in 2025.
To reclaim that position, Leonardo stated, Indonesia must boost production while enhancing the competitiveness of its products in premium markets.
He also noted that low-carbon aquaculture should be applied across all farmed species, as aquaculture activities directly impact environmental carrying capacity and other economic sectors.
He cited Lake Toba as an example, noting that it serves not only aquaculture, but also transportation, tourism, clean water supply, and hydroelectric power generation.
“These factors must be taken into account. No matter how small a contribution to pollution from aquaculture, it can affect the quality and operations of other economic activities,” he said.
During the visit, the ministry highlighted tilapia farming as an example of low-carbon development practices that could be expanded.
These practices include tailoring feed usage and cage designs to match both fish requirements and environmental carrying capacity. In addition, feed technology has been designed to reduce phosphorus content, helping prevent lake pollution.
As a core pillar of the green economic transformation under the 2025–2045 National Long-Term Development Plan (RPJPN), the ministry is integrating low-carbon and climate-resilient development to foster sustainable economic growth while reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
The initiative aims to cut emissions by 31.89 percent to 43.2 percent by 2030 through targeted interventions in the energy transition, land management, blue carbon ecosystems, the circular economy, green industry, and eco-friendly transportation.
Furthermore, the plan targets a reduction in emission intensity of up to 93.5 percent by 2045.

items.title: Health Ministry expands healthcare services in Papua Highlands
items.summary: The Ministry of Health is strengthening healthcare services across Indonesia, including in the Papua Highlands region, ...
items.body_text:
The ministry’s Director of Referral Healthcare Facilities, Ghotama Airlangga, emphasized in a statement on Saturday that healthcare services should be distributed evenly across Indonesia.
“The Ministry of Health’s future program is to provide equitable healthcare throughout the country, especially in the Papua Highlands region and other parts of Papua,” Airlangga said.
According to him, the ministry is facilitating partnerships between all regional general hospitals in the Papua Highlands and major hospitals across Indonesia to provide treatment for cancer, heart disease, stroke, uronephrology, maternal and child health, tuberculosis, pre-existing diseases (EID), diabetes, gastrohepatology, mental health, and eye diseases.
“We hope that in the future, healthcare services for heart disease, stroke, and other serious illnesses will no longer need to be referred outside the Papua Highlands and can be handled here,” he said.
Airlangga emphasized that the program is part of efforts to ensure equitable healthcare across Indonesia through a mentoring approach that supports healthcare workers in the Papua Highlands and enables them to manage chronic diseases.
“We greatly appreciate the support of the Governor of the Papua Highlands for this mentoring program, which will help further improve and advance healthcare services in the region,” he continued.
He added that eight regional general hospitals in the Papua Highlands will have their accreditation upgraded from Class D to Class C to support the delivery of optimal healthcare services.
“Class C hospitals generally serve as referral centers for community health centers (Puskesmas). These facilities provide more comprehensive specialist medical services, particularly in the four basic specialties, internal medicine, including cardiology, pediatrics, surgery and obstetrics and gynecology,” he explained.

items.title: MAP: Where have system losses been highest from 2021 to 2025?
items.summary: Explore this interactive map to see how high the system losses have been in your area
items.body_text:
System losses remain the talk of the town months after President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. promised to remove them in his 2026 State of the Nation Address last July.
Starting this billing cycle in October, consumers will no longer have to pay value-added tax on the system loss charge.
But that is only 12% of the charge, with the Department of Energy initially saying back in July that the government would need about a year to fully remove the system loss charge.
This means the Marcos administration has a long way to go before its vow is fulfilled â and with power rates continuing to be sky-high in many parts of the country due to thin electricity supply, the continuing charge has only become more controversial.
So, what are these losses? In short, system loss refers to the cost of power that is wasted as it travels from generation sources to homes and buildings.
Currently, this cost is solely paid for by consumers, which means we are paying for electricity that we did not consume.
These losses can be categorized into three types. Some come from the physics of electrical transmission through metal wires, transformers, and gears that convert a small fraction of that power into heat. Others are the result of human interference or error.
So, how bad have system losses actually been? They differ depending on your distribution utility (DU). Explore this interactive map to see how high the distribution system loss has been in your area from 2021 to 2025, based on annual data the ERC required distribution utilities to submit in August 2026.
Rural DUs record highest system losses
Many of the DUs that consistently recorded the highest annual system losses are rural electric cooperatives on the outskirts of Mindanao, Mimaropa, and Bicol regions.
The Philippine Rural Electric Cooperatives Association (PHILRECA) said high system losses in these rural distribution networks can be traced back to extended feeder lines and challenging terrain that are âgoverned by the law of thermodynamics rather than inefficiency.â
Aging infrastructure also plays a role in these losses, with electric cooperatives long suffering from this problem. But modernizing these assets is not so simple, since PHILRECA had previously said these cooperatives suffer from delays in disbursing capital expenditures and fiscal challenges.
Feeder losses most common, but non-technical losses preventable
While feeder technical loss makes up the largest share of system losses overall, individual DUs with some of the highest losses also have a large percentage of non-technical losses.
Advocate groups such as the Institute for Climate Sustainable Cities (ICSC) have long pointed out that these non-technical losses are preventable â and even the unavoidable technical losses can still be managed.
For them, resolving the system loss issue lies in balancing two objectives. The first is to make sure the DUs can recover prudent and efficient costs necessary to provide safe, reliable, and continuous service. The second is to protect consumers from costs coming from inefficiency, inadequate controls, or preventable losses.
âCost recovery should follow performance,â the ICSC said in a separate position paper. âPersistent underperformance, weak loss prevention efforts, or failure to address preventable losses should not automatically result in recoverable charges.â â Rappler.com
    Coding for this layout was done with the assistance of AI.

items.title: These former inmates turn life behind bars into art
items.summary: For the formerly incarcerated members of the Bagongbuhay Group of Artists, art becomes one way of confronting the difficulty of rebuilding life after release
items.body_text:
AT A GLANCE
- The mural 'Buyon' at the UP College of Law, created by the Bagongbuhay Group of Artists, reflects the experiences of former Persons Deprived of Liberty (PDLs) and highlights their lives during and after incarceration.
- The artwork serves as a reminder of the human stories behind the criminal justice system, emphasizing the importance of empathy and understanding for those affected by it.
- The artists express a desire for society to recognize the skills and humanity of former inmates, advocating for second chances and the continuation of art as a means of rehabilitation and connection.
At the UP College of Law, a mural tells a story that cannot be found in a case file.
Painted by members of the Bagongbuhay Group of Artists (BAGA), a collective of former Persons Deprived of Liberty (PDLs), the artwork brings their experiences of detention, change, and life after incarceration into a place where law is taught and practiced.
The painting, Buyon, was formally turned over to the UP College of Law on September 18 as part of the UP Law Class of 2001’s 25th anniversary celebration. It was unveiled alongside a wider exhibit of works by BAGA, a group founded in 2021 that brings together former PDLs and marginalized communities through art.
But before it became a mural hanging inside Bocobo Hall, “buyon” was a word rooted in the everyday reality of life inside detention. It refers to a shared space where PDLs bathe, wash their clothes and dishes, and wait for their turn to use the limited water available.
And behind the painting are the stories of the men who created it — what they remember, what they experienced, and what they are trying to communicate through art.
From jail space to mural
The mural began last year, when Joey de Leon, 57, the founder and president of BAGA, was called to a meeting through Justice Karl Miranda.
Alumni of the UP Law Class of 2001 wanted a large, painting-style mural about the country’s criminal justice system for their legacy project, and they wanted BAGA’s help bringing it to life.
De Leon, who has lived through incarceration himself and would later become one of the five BAGA artists credited on the finished work, proposed starting somewhere the public rarely thinks to look.
“Ang buyon ay isang facility sa loob ng bawat brigada sa kulungan. Doon kayo naliligo, doon rin kayo naglalaba, doon rin dumudumi. Hindi siya katulad ng normal na comfort room o bathroom, pinagsama-sama lahat doon,” De Leon said.
(The buyon is a facility inside every brigada in a detention center. That’s where you bathe, where you wash clothes, and where you relieve yourself. It isn’t like a normal comfort room or bathroom. Everything happens in the same space.)
In the mural, that cramped space is filled with the routines PDLs share. Men bathe and wash clothes beside basins and buckets, against tiled walls and beneath a small barred window. The exhibit’s description also presents the buyon as a place of connection and shared experience among the people who use it. Still, De Leon is careful about what the painting is and is not trying to say.
“Hindi namin sinasabi na, ‘oy, eto kami, bigyan niyo kami,’ kasi may problema ang gobyerno,” he said. “Kami ay pangkaraniwang inmate na naranasan mismo iyon. Pinapakita lang namin, we are humans.”
(We’re not saying, “hey, here we are, give us something,” just because the government has problems. We’re ordinary inmates who lived through it ourselves. We’re just showing that we are humans.)
Making something after detention
For Danilo Faustino, 65, the harder question came after his release. What happens after you have served your sentence?
Faustino spent around two decades in the New Bilibid Prison. For him and other members of BAGA, art became one way of confronting the difficulty of rebuilding life after release. Finding regular work can be difficult for former PDLs, particularly for someone his age, and painting offered another way to earn and help support his family. He wants the

items.title: Converge package offers 0% commission fees for 3 months on TikTok Shop
items.summary: Converge ICT Solutions, DTI, and TikTok Shop launch SellerPlus, offering new online sellers a three-month commission-free period and essential tools to boost their e-commerce ventures
items.body_text:
AT A GLANCE
- Converge ICT Solutions, DTI, and TikTok Shop launched SellerPlus, a package offering new online sellers and livestreamers a three-month break from commission fees.
- SellerPlus provides a 200 Mbps fiber connection, access to TikTok Shop tools, and features like 0% commission for the first 90 days, customer service support, and gamified incentives.
- The initiative also includes mentorship through BizFriend PH and access to training facilities, aimed at supporting micro, small, and medium enterprises in leveraging social commerce and livestreaming.
MANILA, Philippines – New online sellers and livestreamers can get a three-month break from commission fees under a new package launched by Converge ICT Solutions, the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI), and TikTok Shop.
Called SellerPlus, the package is aimed at micro, small, and medium enterprises, home-based businesses, and creators looking to build their businesses through livestream and e-commerce. It combines a 200 Mbps Converge fiber connection with TikTok Shop tools and other services.
Among its more useful features for sellers just starting out is 0% commission fees for their first 90 days on TikTok Shop, potentially allowing newly onboarded merchants to keep more of their sales while they establish an audience and test their products online.
The package also gives merchants access to vouchers and incentives through a gamified goal system called “seller missions,” promises dedicated customer service support, and traffic and voucher support through TikTok Shop’s monthly Sariling Atin campaign, which promotes local brands.
Converge said the 200 Mbps fiber connection is intended to support uninterrupted livestreaming, highlighting that disruptions with poor connections can lead to lost sales. The package also includes personal accident insurance from AXA.
SellerPlus is also tied to the DTI’s AI and Scale-Up Center in Makati, where entrepreneurs can access co-working facilities, training spaces, digital skills workshops, and demonstrations of tools such as content generators, customer-service bots, and inventory software.
SellerPlus also includes a mentorship component through BizFriend PH, a Facebook community where local merchants can exchange experiences, collaborate, and receive business advice. The program’s BizPro Rockstar Mentorship Program brings in experts in areas such as partnership law, digital marketing, tax compliance, business communication, and business growth.
The initiative comes as more small businesses use social commerce and livestreaming as lower-cost ways to reach customers. For newer sellers in particular, temporarily removing commission fees — alongside internet access, promotional support, and training — could reduce some of the upfront costs of experimenting with online selling. – Rappler.com

items.title: Sara Duterte camp hits Trillanes over ‘desperate, tired narratives’
items.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte's spokesperson Salvador Paolo Panelo Jr. on Saturday, October 3, hit former senator Antonio Trillanes IV over allegations linking the vice president's family to Chinese funds, calling them “desperate and tired narratives.”
items.body_text:
Sara Duterte camp hits Trillanes over ‘desperate, tired narratives’
MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte's spokesperson Salvador Paolo Panelo Jr. on Saturday, October 3, hit former senator Antonio Trillanes IV over allegations linking the vice president's family to Chinese funds, calling them “desperate and tired narratives.”
Panelo issued the statement a day after Trillanes alleged that a food company partly owned by Duterte's husband, lawyer Manases “Mans” Carpio, received more than P319 million from China.
“Since 2016, former Senator Antonio Trillanes IV has been peddling the same exhausted lies regarding Extrajudicial Killings (EJKs), fabricated drug links, imaginary unexplained wealth, baseless corruption allegations, and fictional China connections against the Duterte family,” Panelo said.
Trillanes' China allegations
Trillanes made the allegations at a press conference on Friday, October 2, a day after House prosecutors dropped him as a witness in Duterte's impeachment trial.
He said he had asked to be removed from the witness list to relieve the prosecution of further pressure and instead disclose publicly what he intended to present before the senator-judges.
Trillanes alleged that Chinese government-linked entities and corporations sent more than P319 million to Cale88 Foods Corp., a banana chip exporter where Carpio was an incorporator, director and shareholder from 2021 to 2024.
Securities and Exchange Commission Director Gerardo Del Rosario previously testified during the impeachment proceedings that Carpio's stake in Cale88 rose to 47.5% in 2024 before disappearing in 2025.
Duterte herself had no ownership interest in Cale88, but Trillanes argued that the company's ties to her husband were relevant to her liability.
He also presented records showing that the Tapang at Malasakit Alliance for the Philippines Inc., a nonprofit founded by Duterte, received P150 million from the Embassy of the People's Republic of China.
The group's financial statement showed that the money was a donation intended to build 13 classroom buildings in Davao City. The project was carried out under an agreement with the Chinese embassy and coordinated with the Department of Education.
On Thursday, lead prosecutor Rep. Jinky Luistro confirmed that Anti-Money Laundering Council records submitted to the impeachment court included summaries of remittances to Cale88 from China and other countries. She declined to disclose the amounts, citing the court's sub judice rule.

“Yet, the moment he was faced with the very first opportunity to test his wild claims against actual facts, verified records, and law through cross-examination by the Vice President’s defense team, Trillanes folded,” Panelo said.
“Instead of defending his claims under oath, he chose the comfort of a safe and scripted press conference where his lies could once again go unchallenged.”
Panelo also brought up Trillanes' previous allegations involving extrajudicial killings, alleged drug links and supposed unexplained wealth against the Duterte family.
He cited Peter Joemel Advincula, alias “Bikoy,” lawyer Jude Sabio and Arturo Lascañas, whom he described as people Trillanes previously relied on to support his claims.
Panelo claimed that Advincula had admitted being used in a destabilization plot and that Sabio had withdrawn his communication to the International Criminal Court.
He also said Lascañas' credibility had been “completely demolished” by contradictions in his statements.

items.title: ICC allows prior testimony of witness in Rodrigo Duterte case
items.summary: The International Criminal Court has allowed prosecutors to introduce the prior recorded testimony of a witness in the crimes against humanity of murder trial of former president Rodrigo Duterte.
items.body_text:
ICC allows prior testimony of witness in Rodrigo Duterte case
MANILA, Philippines — The International Criminal Court has allowed prosecutors to introduce the prior recorded testimony of a witness in the crimes against humanity of murder trial of former president Rodrigo Duterte.
In a decision dated October 2, Trial Chamber III granted the prosecution's request to introduce the written statement of the witness, identified as P-1100, under Rule 68(3) of the ICC Rules of Procedure and Evidence.
The Chamber said the admission of the testimony would not prejudice Duterte's rights or the fairness of the proceedings.
“Rule 68(3) of the Rules does not replace oral testimony but, rather, complements it, and the Defence will have full opportunity to question P-1100 on any issues relating to his testimony,” the Chamber said.
The decision is a preliminary ruling and remains subject to P-1100 appearing before the Chamber and consenting to the introduction of his written statement.
The prosecution had said P-1100's testimony is relevant to its allegations involving a policy to "neutralise" alleged criminals in the Philippines through violent crimes, including murder.
It also said the witness's evidence concerns the alleged modus operandi of the Davao Death Squad and Duterte's individual criminal responsibility, including his knowledge and intent.
The ICC noted that P-1100's testimony was expected to be corroborative of evidence from other witnesses who are scheduled to testify in person.
The prosecution had asked to conduct a two-hour supplementary examination of P-1100 instead of a full examination, which it estimated would take seven hours.
The Chamber, however, said two hours was excessive.
“The Chamber finds the requested amount of time to be excessive given the nature and content of P-1100’s evidence and defeats the purpose of Rule 68(3) of the Rules,” the decision read.
It ordered the prosecution to streamline its questioning and complete its examination of P-1100 within one hour.
Defense opposed admission
Duterte's defense had asked the Chamber to reject the prosecution's request.
The defense argued that P-1100's evidence predates the charged period and questioned whether the witness had sufficient factual basis to support the broader propositions for which his evidence was being offered.
It also argued that introducing the testimony could result in lengthy cross-examination, potentially taking the proceedings away from the matters actually in dispute.
The Chamber was not persuaded.
It said P-1100's testimony appeared relevant to the background and context of the case.
“Although P-1100’s prior recorded testimony contains some opinion statements, the Defence will have the opportunity to question the witness, including to test the basis of P-1100’s knowledge, to probe the foundation for the interpretations he offers, and to elicit the limits of what he is, and is not, able to say from personal observation,” the Chamber said.
It said questions about the weight to be given to P-1100's testimony would be considered later.
The Chamber said it would assess the "probative value" of the witness's testimony, including the basis of his knowledge, as part of its overall assessment when deliberating on the judgment.
ICC rejects 4 supporting materials
While the Chamber allowed P-1100's written testimony, it rejected four pieces of associated material that the prosecution wanted introduced with it.
These were identified as PHL-OTP-0000-1794, PHL-OTP-0000-1795, PHL-OTP-0000-1796 and PHL-OTP-0000-1799.
The Chamber said the witness did not sufficiently use or explain the materials in his prior recorded testimony for them to form an integral part of his statement.
For PHL-OTP-0000-1799, the Chamber said P-1100 did not refer to the substance of the material and that it was unclear which documents he was referring to.

items.title: Dec. 16 verdict date for Sara Duterte not set by impeachment court — Pangilinan
items.summary: Sen. Francis "Kiko" Pangilinan said the Senate impeachment court has yet to set a date for the verdict in Vice President Sara Duterte's trial, contradicting an announcement by court spokesperson Reginald Tongol that the proceedings could end on December 16.
items.body_text:
Dec. 16 verdict date for Sara Duterte not set by impeachment court — Pangilinan
MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Francis "Kiko" Pangilinan said the Senate impeachment court has yet to set a date for the verdict in Vice President Sara Duterte's trial, contradicting an announcement by court spokesperson Reginald Tongol that the proceedings could end on December 16.
Pangilinan, one of the senator-judges, said the impeachment court has yet to formally or informally discuss a timetable for the trial, including the proposed verdict date.
"I have been asked by the media and the public about the schedule of the trial and the verdict date," Pangilinan said in a statement posted on Facebook Saturday.
"The Impeachment Court has yet to formally or informally discuss this and has yet to decide on the timetable/timeline of the trial moreso a verdict date of December 16," he added.
Tongol said Friday that the impeachment court was increasingly confident it could finish the trial before the Senate's holiday recess, with a final verdict targeted for December 16.
He said the trial had moved ahead of its initial calendar after the House prosecution panel dropped several witnesses from its original lineup.
The prosecution could finish presenting its evidence for Article II, which covers alleged ill-gotten wealth, by next week, Tongol said.
The trial will go on recess after October 15 and resume on November 23. Once the prosecution rests, the defense is expected to present its evidence within 30 days.
Pangilinan, however, stressed that Tongol's December 16 announcement should not be treated as a decision of the impeachment court.
"This verdict date is merely the opinion of the spokesperson. As Senator Judge, I do not share the opinion of the spokesperson," Pangilinan said.
"He has no authority to issue his personal opinions on the Court’s behalf," he added.
The impeachment trial involves allegations against Duterte, including accusations of unexplained wealth.
The prosecution is also set to present evidence involving P6.7 billion in transactions linked to the bank accounts of Duterte and her husband, Manases Carpio.
The court recently postponed the testimony of Anti-Money Laundering Council executive director Ronel Buenaventura after the defense sought additional time to review documents submitted by the agency.

items.title: Whistleblowing teacher exposes kindergarten cooks washing mops in wok used for children's meals
items.summary: Authorities in the Chinese city of Nanjing have removed a kindergarten principal and disciplined 11 officials after a former teacher reported that cooks washed mops and drain covers in the wok used for children's meals.
items.body_text:
A joint investigation team in Nanjing's Jiangbei New Area said on Sept. 22 that kitchen surveillance footage and interviews confirmed "serious problems" with hygiene management at the Affiliated Kindergarten of Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology, Xinhua reported.
The principal, surnamed Zou, deliberately concealed problems in the canteen and failed to fix them, while the deputy principal in charge of logistics, surnamed Qin, neglected day-to-day management, the team found. Both were removed from their posts and a cook surnamed Zhang was fired.
Eleven officials from Pancheng subdistrict, the area's market regulation bureau and its education bureau received penalties including serious intra-party warnings and major administrative demerits for failing to respond effectively when children fell ill and for weak follow-up supervision.
The team apologized to the affected children and their parents.
The children became ill on June 30, the last day of the spring semester, with nausea and vomiting during and after lunch.
The former teacher, whom The Beijing News identified by the pseudonym Wang Chang, was the kindergarten's health teacher and canteen safety officer at the time. She told the newspaper she estimated on the day that 40 to 50 children were unwell, and that pupils in five classes showed symptoms.
Parents repeatedly asked the kindergarten for the cause but had received no formal answer by the time the new term began in September.
Wang resigned on Sept. 11 after a dispute with the principal. Three days later she filed a complaint with the area's discipline inspection commission and posted on WeChat and Xiaohongshu that cooks washed mops and drain covers in the wok, used washing sinks interchangeably, and soaked mosquito nets in disinfectant and scrubbed shoes in the vegetable sink.
She said she had reported the violations to the kindergarten's management many times since joining in August 2022, to no effect.
"I had misgivings, because I might not be able to find work after going public. But if I said nothing, I would feel guilty," she told The Beijing News, adding that she weighed the decision for two days and two nights.
The university's publicity department filed a complaint seeking the removal of her Xiaohongshu post, arguing that she had published problems the kindergarten had already fixed and misled parents, according to Wang.
On Sept. 16, parents who demanded to see surveillance recordings found footage from June 29, the day before the children fell ill, showing a mop being washed in the wok, she said.
The cause of the vomiting had still not been determined as of Sept. 23, Jiemian News reported.
A parent told the outlet that the kindergarten has since replaced its principal and kitchen team. The public kindergarten opened in September 2022 as a joint project between the university and Jiangbei New Area, and had about 300 children in 10 classes at the end of last semester.
Some Chinese internet users have demanded criminal charges, but Guo Xueliang, a lawyer at Beijing Zhicheng Law Firm, told Jiemian News that the evidence made public so far does not meet the threshold for a conviction, though the kindergarten and the individuals involved should bear administrative liability.
Wang expects to struggle to find another job and plans to try running a street stall once the case is settled.
"I know I spoke up very late, but I hope that at least the children there now and those who enroll later can eat a clean meal," she said.

items.title: Singaporean tourist asks for help lifting his bike, gets mocked by Swiss resident with slant-eye gesture
items.summary: A Singaporean livestreamer recently shared how he got a racist slant-eye gesture after asking a man in the Swiss village of Giswil for help lifting his fallen bike during his first motorcycle trip through Europe.
items.body_text:
The rider, who goes by Sukas online, was streaming live on the platform Kick when his motorcycle toppled over on a private meadow in the central canton of Obwalden, Swiss news site 20 Minuten reported. The man asked if he had missed the no-entry sign at the start of the path.
When Sukas apologized and said he had not seen it, the man twisted his face and pulled his eyes into slits. Sukas called the gesture racist, and the man replied that he hoped the motorcycle was broken.
The man took photos of the bike and the streamer rather than helping. Once the bike was upright, Sukas told viewers the man was a racist and that he could not understand such a reaction, 20 Minuten reported, adding that it verified the footage's location using Google Maps.
Speaking later to Singaporean news site Mothership, Sukas, 37, said he was not offended "one single bit" and that the man had looked comical with his tongue sticking out.
The man, who Sukas said lived nearby, considered the area off-limits because of the sign.
Sukas has ridden in Malaysia and Thailand several times, but this is his first ride in Europe, he told Mothership. His tour has taken him through Switzerland, Austria and Germany, streamed almost nonstop to several thousand viewers a day, according to 20 Minuten.
The clip has since spread across social media, drawing a response Sukas described as polarizing. Some Swiss people apologized, while others said he should not ride a bike he cannot lift, or that he deserved it in a "country of rules and extremely hefty fines," a label Sukas, as a Singaporean, should find familiar.
Many social media users wrote that the man was a poor advertisement for Switzerland and Obwalden. Swiss comedian Ahmet Bilge called his behavior disgusting and racist in a TikTok video.
Switzerland ranked first of 100 countries in U.S. News & World Report's 2026 Best Countries rankings, released in May, leading the governance and economic development categories.
Sukas told those who apologized not to do so on behalf of an unrelated individual, and praised their country. Some Swiss residents in Singapore have offered to buy him meals and invited him to events.
He plans to return to Singapore before setting off in December on a ride to China's Yunnan Province. His dream, he told Mothership, is to ride from Singapore to Western Europe.

items.title: Passenger escorted off flight at Singapore Changi airport over cardboard box dispute
items.summary: A woman was escorted off a Batik Air flight at Singapore's Changi Airport after refusing to hand a large cardboard box to cabin crew, delaying departure by about an hour.
items.body_text:
The standoff took place on flight OD804 to Kuala Lumpur, which was due to leave Changi's Terminal 4 at 12:30 p.m. on Sept. 30, Singapore's Shin Min Daily News reported, citing a passenger surnamed Ke.
Ke, 42, who works in property management, said the woman appeared to be in her 20s and sat in an aisle seat in the middle of the cabin, holding a box almost as large as a carry-on suitcase.
The box did not fit in the overhead bin, and crew told her she could not keep it on her lap, Ke said.
Flight attendants repeatedly asked her to let them store it, with one promising it would be returned on landing, but she refused, Ke told the newspaper.
A male flight attendant eventually carried the box away, but the woman stayed in her seat.
About five police officers then boarded and tried to persuade her to cooperate before leading her off the plane, about 45 minutes after the crew first approached her, Ke said.
The box bore a red "fragile" label, according to Malaysia's Oriental Daily.
TikTok user minimanimo posted a video of the incident on Sept. 30. According to the post, the woman insisted on keeping the box under the seat in front of her, declined a flight attendant's offer to put it on an empty seat and refused to fasten her seatbelt.
The footage shows a flight attendant carrying the box toward the front of the plane, then uniformed officers standing in the aisle around a seat before a woman follows them out.
Flight leaves an hour late
The Boeing 737-800 took off at 1:29 p.m., 59 minutes behind schedule, and landed in Kuala Lumpur at 2:15 p.m., according to Flightradar24 data.
Passengers were given two bottles of mineral water as compensation, Ke said.
Kuala Lumpur-Singapore was the world's third-busiest international air route in 2025 with 5.6 million scheduled seats, according to aviation data firm OAG.

items.title: Flood-battered Bangkok amusement park won’t rule out sale
items.summary: The management of Siam Amazing Park is desperately seeking a way to keep the 46-year-old amusement and water park operating after flooding in Bangkok damaged nearly the entire complex, with a sale for 10 billion baht one of many options.
items.body_text:
The management of Siam Amazing Park is desperately seeking a way to keep the 46-year-old amusement and water park operating after flooding in Bangkok damaged nearly the entire complex, with a sale for 10 billion baht one of many options.
Many water pumps have been deployed around the park, also known as Suansiam, which covers about 300 rai in Khan Na Yao district, as work continued on Saturday to drain floodwater and restore facilities.
Extensive damage affecting nearly 100% of the complex was reported following the park’s announcement on Wednesday that it would close for six months.
Initial damage has been estimated at more than 500 million baht, according to the management.
Chaiwat Luangamornlert, the chairman and founder of Siam Amazing Park, described the situation as the worst flood he has experienced in his 90 years, saying it had submerged every inch of the park he built with his own hands.
Speaking to media visiting the park on Saturday, he said the water inundated the site rapidly within a single day, leaving insufficient time to prepare or take preventive measures because staff had not received advance information about the situation.
Mr Chaiwat said in a video posted on the park’s online page that he knew there had been heavy rain but did not expect it to be this severe.
Chaiwat Luangamornlert, chairman and founder of Siam Amazing Park, in 2015. (Bangkok Post file photo)
The damage is so extensive that resuming operations will take a long time, particularly as its rides use electrical and electronic systems imported from overseas.
The park is currently coordinating with the manufacturers to bring in engineering teams to inspect the rides and assess their safety.
Management initially said restoration could take three to four months, but several factors will determine the park’s future, including government assistance, support from financial institutions and public response.
The park employs more than 500 people. Mr Chaiwat said many had come to cry with him, uncertain about how they would get by during the closure.
He told the media that if there were interested parties willing to take over the business, Siam Amazing Park was prepared to sell it for about 10 billion baht, excluding its more than 30 rides.
One other option under consideration is selling tickets in advance, with the proceeds used to restore and improve the facilities.
Management said the plan was intended to raise revenue for the rehabilitation of the business and that it did not want to solicit donations, hoping the measure would help the park reopen as soon as possible.
The park also operates a zoo, where 10 hog deer were rescued from the flood on Sept 27, while six others were found dead in the water.
Animals that survived the flood have been handed over to the Zoological Park Organisation, while domestic animals were sent to Wat Pa Phutthachinwongsaram in Phayao province for further care.
Siam Amazing Park was founded in November 1980 and remains the oldest amusement and water park complex in Southeast Asia. It is also known locally as the “Bangkok Sea” for its large artificial sea, which suffered extensive flood damage and will require major renovation work.
A boy has fun at the Maha Songkran Siam event at Siam Amazing Park in 2024. (Bangkok Post file photo)

items.title: Bangkok’s iconic buses to live on after surviving floods
items.summary: Bangkok’s iconic cream-red buses will live on, with selected vehicles to be repurposed for emergency reserves after the ageing fleet proved its worth transporting passengers during the 2026 flood, says the director of the Bangkok Mass Transit Authority (BMTA).
items.body_text:
Bangkok’s iconic cream-red buses will live on, with selected vehicles to be repurposed for emergency reserves after the ageing fleet proved its worth transporting passengers during the 2026 flood, says the director of the Bangkok Mass Transit Authority (BMTA).
“I will not abandon our cream-red buses,” Kittikan Chomdoung Charuworapolkul declared in a post on Facebook on Friday.
The BMTA is moving towards cleaner transport, with more than 1,500 electric buses set to replace the ageing vehicles from 2027.
However, the recent major floods showed that the cream-red buses remain essential during crises and emergencies, Mr Kittikan said.
The buses can operate through water as deep as 80 centimetres in emergencies, while their conventional fuel systems allow them to be refuelled at the scene and continue operating.
“This is a level of durability that modern systems are still hard-pressed to replace,” he said.
Mr Kittikan said the challenge was to revive the cream-red buses by applying engineering solutions. Only vehicles that remain structurally sound would be selected for a major overhaul, including a complete cleaning and refurbishment of their systems.
Their engines would also be upgraded to meet modern emissions standards, as the buses have long faced criticism over visible exhaust smoke.
The refurbished buses would no longer operate on regular routes but would instead serve as “emergency reserve buses” to be deployed when needed.
Mr Kittikan also invited the public to share ideas about what colour scheme or symbol should be used to reflect the buses’ new role.
Bus No. 59 on duty on the Rangsit-Sanam Luang route during recent flooding. (Photo: Kittikan Chomdoung Charuworapolkul)
The cream-red bus fleet celebrated its 35th anniversary in Bangkok on Aug 2.
The buses currently operated by the BMTA are second-generation models with centrally positioned doors. The first batch was officially handed over and launched in 1991.
At the time, four models of non-air-conditioned buses were introduced — Hino, Isuzu, Daewoo and Mitsubishi — along with Mercedes-Benz Padane cream-and-blue air-conditioned buses, for a combined total of 2,040 vehicles, according to Bangkokbusclub, an online community and information hub for Bangkok bus fans and commuters.
However, problems with maintenance contracts led to the earlier retirement of the Daewoo and Mercedes-Benz Padane buses.
The fleet now consists of three cream-red models, with 1,519 buses in service, excluding spare vehicles: 490 Hino AK176s, 529 Isuzu MT111QBs and 500 Mitsubishi Fuso RP118s.
The BMTA plans to gradually retire the cream-red buses once it receives new electric air-conditioned buses under a vehicle rental contract previously signed with Nakhonchai Air.
“We are bringing back a BMTA icon and giving it value in a new mission that is more challenging than before,” Mr Kittikan wrote.
Some commenters on his post also expressed hope that the BMTA would continue operating some cream-red buses on regular routes, citing concerns about higher fares for electric air-conditioned services.
Kittikan Chomdoung Charuworapolkul, director of the Bangkok Mass Transit Authority (BMTA), stands in floodwaters among the remaining ancient passenger buses. (Photo: Kittikan Chomdoung Charuworapolkul)

items.title: Crusader for crime victims faces money-laundering charges
items.summary: Cybercrime police arrested crime victims’ rights activist Atchariya Ruengrattanapong outside a boxing stadium in Samut Sakhon on Saturday on charges including money laundering.
items.body_text:
Cybercrime police arrested crime victims’ rights activist Atchariya Ruengrattanapong outside a boxing stadium in Samut Sakhon on Saturday on charges including money laundering.
Investigators said they had received complaints that the high-profile lawyer used money donated by the public to his organisation to bet on Muay Thai fights.
Officers from the Cyber Crime Investigation Bureau (CCIB) apprehended Mr Atchariya in front of the Siam Om Noi boxing stadium in Krathum Baen district at noon on Saturday, said Pol Lt Gen Thinnakorn Rangmat, the CCIB commissioner.
Mr Atchariya was wanted on an arrest warrant issued by the Criminal Court on charges of fraud, inputting false computer data, money laundering and illegal gambling, said Pol Maj Gen Prasong Chalermphan, commander of CCIB Division 1.
According to the arresting team, Mr Atchariya portrayed himself as a social activist fighting for justice while using public trust as a means to launder money and channel funds into online boxing gambling networks, with transactions worth hundreds of millions of of baht.
The investigation grew out of cases handled by the Bueng Kum police station and CCIB Division 1, which had dismantled online gambling networks operating through the “Muay Phak Yok Variety” and “Phak Yok Variety Investment Deposit” Line groups. Investigators said financial records provided strong evidence linking Mr Atchariya to the networks. Two bank accounts linked to the activist recorded combined transactions of more than 350 million baht, they said.
His personal Kasikornbank account recorded 1,196 transactions worth 191 million baht from January 2024 to April 2025. Another Kbank account in the name of the Crime Victims Assistance Club recorded 5,140 transactions worth 168 million baht from May 2013 to April 2026.
Several complainants said they had been persuaded by advertisements on social media to donate money because they believed the club was helping society and fighting injustice. Some alleged they were threatened by Mr Atchariya after he learned they were planning to file complaints, said the arresting team.
Police are expanding the investigation to identify other people allegedly involved and take legal action against them, Pol Maj Gen Prasong said. (Story continues below)
Police escort crime victims’ rights activist Atchariya Ruengrattanapong after he was arrested outside the Siam Om Noi boxing stadium in Samut Sakhon on Saturday. (Photo supplied/Wassayos Ngamkham)
Extortion allegations
In April this year, Mr Atchariya was granted bail after being charged in connection with an alleged 2.5-million-baht extortion plot targeting people involved in the justice process.
The case arose from complaints brought by an immigration police officer who said he was pressured to pay money to prevent Mr Atchariya from posting allegations that he was involved in the illegal removal of Chinese detainees from a detention centre.
Last year, Mr Atchariya staged a high-profile public campaign exposing alleged corruption linking police officers, politicians and online gambling networks. He claimed that financial flows from the BNK Master network involved over 30 police officers and multiple politicians.

items.title: Sixth arrest, same mystery: UK-Iranian man out on bail over RAF Fairford scare
items.summary: LONDON, Oct 3 — A UK-Iranian dual national arrested over a mysterious incident near a British military airbase has...
items.body_text:
LONDON, Oct 3 — A UK-Iranian dual national arrested over a mysterious incident near a British military airbase has been released on bail, counter-terrorism police said on Saturday.
The 25-year-old was arrested in central London on Thursday “on suspicion of preparation of terrorist acts” as part of an investigation into events near RAF Fairford in southwest England on Sunday.
Five other men arrested on suspicion of explosives and terrorism offences near the airbase in Gloucestershire were also released on bail earlier this week.
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said there were “strong indications that Iran played a part” in the incident, a claim Tehran has rejected.
But the source and nature of the threat near the airbase – used by the US military in its war against Iran – have remained shrouded in mystery.
Police were called to the base early on Sunday after reports that “suspicious” white vans were heading towards it, triggering the evacuation of a nearby village and the declaration of a “major incident”.
Days later, police said no explosives had been found at the scene.
Adding to the mystery, British media reported that officers were alerted to the incident by one of the initial suspects, although police have not commented on the reports.
Washington has further muddied the waters by criticising the release of the suspects on bail and declaring hostile state involvement early in the investigation.
“The investigation into the circumstances surrounding events in Gloucestershire is continuing,” UK police said in an update on Saturday. — AFP

items.title: ‘Unacceptable’: US Muslim group demands action from Trump over American teen held for months without charge in Israel
items.summary: WASHINGTON, Oct 3 — The Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR) yesterday called on the White House and Congr...
items.body_text:
WASHINGTON, Oct 3 — The Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR) yesterday called on the White House and Congress to demand the release of Abdalkareem Issa Ahmed Safi, an American teenager held in an Israeli prison for nearly four months without charge, Anadolu Ajansi (AA) reported.
“It should be unacceptable to the White House and Congress for the Israeli government to continue kidnapping Americans and disappearing them into prisons known for torture, all without any criminal charges or other due process,” Nihad Awad, CAIR’s national executive director, said in a statement.
“The Trump administration has a legal and moral obligation to protect American citizens overseas, especially from rogue governments funded by American taxpayer dollars,” he added.
Awad urged Congress “to exercise its oversight authority and demand that the State Department secure Abdalkareem’s swift and safe release.”
CAIR and its chapter in the state of Texas said Safi, a US citizen with roots in Texas, has been “held hostage in an Israeli prison known for torture for almost four months without facing any criminal charges.”
According to a statement from the US-based American Muslims for Palestine, Israeli forces this June raided Safi’s family home in Jalazone, north of the city of Ramallah in the occupied West Bank, in the middle of the night.
The group said Safi is the third Palestinian American citizen detained by Israeli forces without charge or trial, alongside Sama Safi and Adam Karakrah.
According to a report by US-based independent news outlet Zeteo, Israeli authorities issued an administrative detention order against him days later, based on information withheld from his lawyer and family. The practice allows Israel to hold detainees without charge or trial.
Asked about the case, a US State Department spokesman told Anadolu that the department is “aware of reports of an American detained in the West Bank.”
“The Trump Administration takes its commitment to assist Americans abroad seriously, and we are tracking the situation,” the spokesman said.
“When Americans are detained abroad, the Department works on their behalf to obtain access to adequate medical care, proper treatment, and regular consular visits,” the spokesman added.
The spokesman said the administration “has no higher priority than the safety and security of Americans,” but declined to comment further, citing “privacy and other considerations.” — Bernama-Anadolu

items.title: Flydubai co-pilot tried to carry out ‘terrorist act’, attacked captain with cockpit axe, UAE says
items.summary: DUBAI, Oct 3 — UAE investigators have said the co-pilot of a flydubai flight to Israel this week was planning a &l...
items.body_text:
DUBAI, Oct 3 — UAE investigators have said the co-pilot of a flydubai flight to Israel this week was planning a “terrorist act” and used the cockpit’s emergency axe to attack the captain, but they did not reveal his motive.
Initial findings from the UAE’s investigation into the attack also did not confirm his nationality, according to a report today from the country’s state news agency WAM, but a Saudi source has confirmed to AFP that he was Omani.
Media reports have also said he had been barred from flying in his home nation over concerns about extremist views.
The reports came as the first flight carrying Israelis home from the United Arab Emirates landed in Tel Aviv after services were suspended following the attack, according to Israel’s airport authority website.
“The co-pilot had attempted to carry out a terrorist act” and had “attacked the captain in the cockpit with the emergency axe and tried to take control of the aircraft”, WAM quoted UAE Attorney General Hamad Saif Al Shamsi as saying, referring to initial findings of an investigation.
The co-pilot is still in custody in the UAE. Multiple media outlets overnight identified him as Omani national Hamam al-Hammami and said he had been banned from flying in Oman over concerns about his extremist views.
During the flydubai flight, the plane’s Indian captain was assaulted by the co-pilot but the captain managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers and crew to overpower the attacker and force an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.
Passengers described rushing the cockpit and a fight for control after the plane plummeted — losing around 17,000 feet of altitude in the span of a minute, according to the Flightradar24 website.
‘Radical indoctrination’
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said the suspect had undergone “Islamist radical indoctrination” and had attempted to crash the plane.
The Wall Street Journal reported yesterday that Omani authorities had banned the pilot from flying over concerns he had adopted radical ideological views, citing people familiar with the matter.
CNN, citing two sources familiar with the matter, reported the pilot was removed from a job at Oman’s national airline last year over concerns about extremist views.
Al Arabiya, citing an informed source, also reported that Omani authorities determined that the co-pilot held extremist views.
The broadcaster said he had spent time in Syria, raising concerns he may have been influenced by radical groups there.
ABC News, citing senior intelligence and law enforcement officials familiar with the investigation, reported the suspect had allegedly been found in possession of extremist materials while he was a trainee.
US President Donald Trump warned on Thursday that if Iran was found to be linked to the attack the country would be “hit very hard”.
Netanyahu has said Israel would check how he had been cleared to work on flights to the country.
“We have constraints that say that you can’t have pilots from countries that don’t have diplomatic relations with Israel. Obviously he was able to go through that,” Netanyahu told Fox News. — AFP

items.title: North Korea's Kim Yo Jong says intermediate-range missile test was conducted
items.body_text:
North Korea's Kim Yo Jong says intermediate-range missile test was conducted
SEOUL: North Korea's Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of leader Kim Jong Un, said in a statement on Saturday (Oct 3) that her country had tested an intermediate-range strategic missile.
The South Korean military said earlier on Saturday that North Korea fired a ballistic missile which flew more than 700km toward the sea off its east coast.
Kim Yo Jong, who is a director of North Korea's ruling party, said a drill of a "strategic weapon" was conducted toward the sea off its east coast using the intermediate-range missile.
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un oversaw the drill which was carried out by "a firepower sub-unit undertaking an exclusive special mission", his sister said.
Citing statements by Seoul and Tokyo regarding how far the missile flew, she said that their results showed the limitations of their tracking capability.
"Whenever we applied the wave-like trajectory mode to missiles, the enemy failed to track the targets from their first skip points," she said, without showing any evidence.
South Korea and Japan also "should acknowledge the speed of the missile", she said without disclosing the speed. The missile was also capable of changing its flight orbit at a low altitude with artificial intelligence technology applied, she added.
"In other words, this means that there is no way to avoid this attack," she said.
North Korea has launched missile tests on more than 10 occasions so far this year. Pyongyang has sometimes said it was testing new types of weapons systems. Some of the tests have come after North Korea protested joint military drills between Seoul and Washington.
The launch came after Kim Yo Jong issued a statement on Friday that dismissed Seoul's demand for an apology for what it said were North Korean mines that seriously wounded South Korean soldiers in the Demilitarized Zone, a heavily fortified area between the two Koreas.

items.title: Hallgrimsson hopes Irish bonds will be stronger after tough period
items.body_text:
Hallgrimsson hopes Irish bonds will be stronger after tough period
Oct 3 : Ireland coach Heimir Hallgrimsson has said his side will come out of the international window stronger after two fractious games against Israel that fans and politicians had called on his side to boycott.
The matches had been under the spotlight since the sides were drawn together in February, with Ireland one of Europe's most outspoken critics of Israel's war in Gaza. There have been numerous protests in Ireland asking for the team not to fulfil the fixtures with Israel.
Such was the opposition to the Irish team playing Israel that the Football Association of Ireland chose to hold the game behind closed doors in Backa Topola, a small Serbian town of around 12,000 people, rather than in Dublin.
Reserve goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu, who declined to be in the squad for the first game against Israel, will again be missing when the two sides meet in Serbia on Sunday, and captain Dara O’Shea will also miss out due to the birth of his child.
“Football-wise, what's to come most of all is to control our focus level and keep the focus on that one (Sunday’s game against Israel), don't lose it,” the Icelandic coach told a press conference on Saturday.
“There's been a lot of emotions from the people in Ireland about this, and obviously that affects the players as well. We want to do good, but it's always going to be a challenge when the environment is as noisy as it is.”
TWO PROTESTS
Thursday’s 2-2 draw with Austria in Dublin was briefly disrupted by two protests, but a superb goal from Troy Parrott against the Austrians and four points from their last two games have dampened the political controversy around the Irish team.
The FAI is continuing to investigate allegations that Irish players Adam Idah and James Abankwah were racially abused in Sunday’s 3-0 win over the Israelis in Hungary.
“It just goes to a process both in our departments and then UEFA to look at,” Hallgrimsson said.
“I think it was something that was reported from both teams. I just hope that we can focus on football and that football will be the winner after this.”
The 59-year-old said the difficulties the team had faced would strengthen them.
“Surviving this camp, coming out of it together as one, would be a massive win for me, that is coming from my heart,” he said.
“I think all the challenges that this team has gone through, all the criticism, yeah, I think just surviving as a group after this game, that will be a big win for me and for this group, (and) for the (football) association.”

items.title: Norris blames Sepang tarmac as McLaren struggle in Bahrain GP qualifying
items.body_text:
Norris blames Sepang tarmac as McLaren struggle in Bahrain GP qualifying
SEPANG, Malaysia, Oct 3 : World champion Lando Norris found himself wrestling with an uncooperative McLaren in Saturday's qualifying for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, attributing his team's struggles to the circuit's unique surface.
Norris qualified sixth-fastest, sixth tenths of a second slower than pole sitter Max Verstappen, but will start fifth after Red Bull's Isack Hadjar received a grid penalty that drops him from third to eighth.
The McLaren driver, who is fourth in the championship, did not mince words about his car's performance on the Sepang tarmac.
"We are just slow. The car's not good enough here," Norris told reporters.
"This tarmac is very different to a lot of other tracks we have been to this year and therefore I think you see Mercedes struggle a lot more today especially, you see Red Bull quicker than they usually are.
"So I think the order has shaken up a little bit and I think we struggle a little bit more than what we were expecting because of the surface."
Norris said he was pleased with his final qualifying lap and felt he had extracted the maximum from the car.
"However, it's clear we are a long way off the pace. My car is struggling with speed on the straights and we've lacked general pace all weekend," he added.
"So starting fifth is not a surprise. We don't expect any miracles and it's obvious the Red Bulls are in a class of their own here."
His team mate Oscar Piastri was seventh fastest but will line up alongside Norris on the third row due to Hadjar's penalty.
"Not quite the session we wanted. We're struggling a bit for pace here. But overall I was reasonably happy with things," Piastri said.
"An extra tenth (of a second) would have been good... We were just not quite quick enough here unfortunately. It's going to be a race where we can do a lot with strategy - and then hopefully pace."

items.title: Two Iranians appear in UK court over alleged plot to target Jews
items.summary: LONDON, Oct 3 - Two Iranian nationals appeared in a London court on Saturday charged with plotting acts of terrorism involving the use of a homemade bomb to attack the Jewish community in northern England at the behest of a figure believed to be based in Iran.
items.body_text:
Two Iranians appear in UK court over alleged plot to target Jews
LONDON, Oct 3 - Two Iranian nationals appeared in a London court on Saturday charged with plotting acts of terrorism involving the use of a homemade bomb to attack the Jewish community in northern England at the behest of a figure believed to be based in Iran.
Rahman Salehi, 34, and Salam Ahmadyan, 36, were arrested on September 20 at the start of Yom Kippur, the holiest day in the Jewish calendar, when they are accused of carrying out "hostile" surveillance on potential Jewish targets in Manchester, prosecutors say.
These targets included the Manchester Jewish Museum and Heaton Park synagogue, the scene of a deadly attack almost a year ago in which two Jewish worshippers were killed, prosecutor Mark Luckett told Westminster Magistrates' Court.
ALLEGED PLOT INVOLVED HOMEMADE DEVICE
"Both defendants are accused of preparing acts of terrorism targeting the Jewish community in Manchester through the use of a homemade explosive device," Luckett said.
He said the men were accused of being in contact with a third party who is alleged to have directed and coordinated the attack planning and provided instructions on how to assemble a homemade device, which prosecutors allege would have been made from chlorine and brake fluid.
"It's assessed that this individual is also an Iranian national and most likely operating from within Iran," Luckett said.
The court was told both men had come to Britain from Europe in small boats. Salehi had arrived in 2020 and had been granted asylum, while Ahmadyan came in 2023 and his asylum claim was still outstanding, Luckett said.
The men did not enter a plea and were remanded in custody until their next hearing at London's Old Bailey court on October 23.
The case comes a week after Britain said Iran was believed to be involved in a suspected plot to target the RAF Fairford air base which the US military has used to carry out raids against targets in Iran, leading to a dual British-Iranian national being arrested on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts.
Police said on Saturday he had been released on police bail while the investigation continues. British counterterrorism police have said the Manchester allegations were not connected in any way to the Fairford investigation.
Iran has rejected accusations of involvement in a number of plots in Britain in recent years, and said allegations it was connected to the Fairford incident were baseless.
Britain has also seen a significant rise in antisemitism since the Hamas attacks on Israel in October 2023 that triggered the subsequent war in Gaza, including a series of attacks on Jewish sites in London earlier this year.
"It is no secret that this country faces a range of serious threats from the Iranian regime," Home Secretary (interior minister) Shabana Mahmood said in a statement.
"They target our Jewish communities and try to silence their critics overseas, often through proxies and criminal networks to hide their involvement." REUTERS
