items.title: Taiwan receives first 2 F-16V Block 70s
items.body_text:
- Taiwan receives first 2 F-16V Block 70s WAITING FOR MORE: The delivery comes amid growing concern in Taiwan about the Trump administration’s commitment to arming Taipei, despite US reassurances
  - Staff writer, with agencies
Taiwan yesterday took delivery of the first two of 66 F-16V Block 70 jets purchased from the US after years of delays, helping to strengthen an air force that has to scramble almost daily to shadow China’s military. The aircraft, bearing tail numbers 6727 and 6728, landed at Chihhang Air Base in Taitung County at about noon after departing from Hawaii and making a stop in Guam. The two fighter jets had been expected to arrive in Taiwan by the end of August, but remained in Hawaii without explanation as US President Donald Trump prepared to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping (習近平) late last month. An F-16V Block 70 fighter jet, one of two delivered to Taiwan from an order of 66 aircraft from the US, arrives at the Chihhang Air Base in Taitung County yesterday. Photo: Yu Tai-lang, Taipei Times The delivery comes amid growing concern in Taiwan about the Trump administration’s commitment to arming Taipei, despite Washington saying there has been no change in policy. President William Lai (賴清德) welcomed the arrival of the two aircraft. “This is an important milestone in strengthening Taiwan’s air defense capabilities. It also demonstrates our resolve to bolster self-defense and ensure peace through strength,” Lai wrote in a social media post. Lai said it was his administration’s “unwavering” goal to preserve peace in the Taiwan Strait, and that investing in national defense, which increases the cost of invading Taiwan and lowers the risk of miscalculation, helps further that aim. Air Force Command said in a statement that it would carry out a planned transition training and gradually complete preparations for the new aircraft to ensure that their operational capabilities are brought online in phases. The F-16V Block 70s would be operated by the 7th Tactical Fighter Wing, which was established on Dec. 1, 2023, it said. The wing is being organized into operational squadrons in three phases, with air and maintenance personnel being sent to the US in batches for transition training, it said. Some of the remaining F-16V Block 70s have reached the stage of being ready for delivery, it said, adding that it would continue coordinating with the US program office and managing the delivery and return of the aircraft to Taiwan according to the planned schedule. Earlier in the day, Minister of National Defense Wellington Koo (顧立雄) told reporters at the Legislative Yuan that “there will be more than two jets delivered this year.” The delivery dates of subsequent F-16V Block 70s would be determined in coordination with the US, he said. Asked where the new F-16Vs would be stationed, Koo said that, in line with the military’s strategy, eastern Taiwan would be an important stronghold for preserving combat power. He did not elaborate. The US approved the sale of 66 F-16Vs and related equipment to Taiwan in 2019 for about US$8 billion. Delivery was expected to begin in 2023 and be completed this year, but delays due to technical issues have pushed the timetable back. The arrival of the first two aircraft yesterday also came almost exactly a week after Trump met Xi in Washington. Trump said after meeting Xi in Beijing in May that he was holding a new US$14 billion package for Taiwan in abeyance, although he did approve one worth US$11 billion in December last year. The F-16Vs have advanced avionics, weapons and radar systems to better counter the Chinese air force, including its stealthy J-20 fighters, though Washington has been unwilling to provide Taiwan its most advanced fighters such as the F-22 or F-35. An upgrade program for Taiwan’s existing F-16s was completed in 2023. items.title: Traffic fines to be fully allocated to road safety
items.body_text:
- Traffic fines to be fully allocated to road safety
  - By Wu Liang-yi and Jake Chung / Staff reporter, with staff writer
The Ministry of Transportation and Communications (MOTC) yesterday announced amendments to the Regulations Governing the Allocation and Use of Road Traffic Fines (道路交通違規罰鍰收入分配及運用辦法) that would increase the proportion of revenue from traffic fines used to improve traffic safety and enforcement from “at least 12 percent” to 100 percent. For traffic citations issued by special municipalities or city and county governments, 75 percent of the revenue goes to the local government. In the six special municipalities, 99 percent of the fines are deposited into the municipal treasury according to regulations. Department of Public Transportation and Supervision Director-General Hu Ti-chi, front, displays placards at a news conference in Taipei yesterday. Photo: CNA Another 24 percent is allocated to the issuing authority to cover operational costs and law-enforcement-related incentives, while the remaining 1 percent goes to the national treasury. The system has often drawn criticism, with some saying that it creates an incentive for local governments to issue more traffic tickets as it boosts municipal revenue. The issue is particularly pronounced in the six special municipalities, where nearly all traffic fines flow into the city’s coffers, critics said. Department of Public Transportation and Supervision Director-General Hu Ti-chi (胡迪琦) said that with the changes, revenue from traffic violations would hopefully go toward ameliorating roads and financing law enforcement efforts. The changes require city and county governments to issue a public report every six months on how they have used money generated from traffic fines, allowing auditors and the public to scrutinize their use, she said, adding that local governments must budget for and spend the funds in accordance with the Budget Act (預算法). If the funds are not used for their designated purposes, competent authorities should demand local governments rectify the situation within a specified period, Hu said. Official statistics show five of the special municipalities leading in collection of traffic fines: New Taipei City, NT$3.67 billion (US$115.3 million); Taipei, NT$3.15 billion; Taichung, NT$2.89 billion, Taoyuan, NT$2.5 billion; and Kaohsiung, NT$2.48 billion. Citing the NT$20.5 billion in revenue generated by fines last year from all local governments, once the new regulations are implemented, an additional NT$18 billion should be available for traffic improvement and road safety, she said. Local governments would be able to flexibly allocate the funds for infrastructure projects in accident-prone areas in their jurisdictions, including upgrading road signs, markings and traffic signals, renovating pedestrian overpasses and underpasses, and installing additional guardrails and traffic mirrors. The new system would be implemented in line with local governments’ budget cycles, and is expected to take effect in 2028, she said.

- Lin wins second straight boxing gold at Asiad
  - Staff writer, with agencies
Taiwanese Olympic champion Lin Yu-ting (林郁婷) yesterday won her second consecutive Asian Games boxing gold, defeating her Chinese opponent in the women’s 60kg final. Lin beat Yang Chengyu (楊成宇) by a unanimous 5-0 decision at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, adding the 60kg title to her 57kg gold from Hangzhou, China, in 2023. “In this competition, I’m like a newborn calf ... or a little white rabbit that has wandered into a great forest,” Lin said. Gold medalist Lin Yu-ting of Taiwan celebrates on the podium after the women’s 60kg boxing event during the Asian Games at Nishio Gymnasium in Nishio, Japan, yesterday. Photo: Mohd Rasfan, AFP “None of my opponents was ordinary. Every one of them was incredibly strong and powerful,” she said. “I don’t think there was a single one of my four bouts where I didn’t end up on the ground at some point. That shows just how difficult this competition was,” she added. Yang said she struggled to cope with the taller Lin’s style. Taiwanese boxer Lin Yu-ting, in red, punches China’s Yang Chengyu in the women’s 60kg gold medal boxing bout during the Asian Games at Nishio Gymnasium in Nishio, Japan, yesterday. Photo: CNA “She is really tall and, in training, we don’t often face someone of that height, so that distance can feel unfamiliar,” she said. The victory gave Taiwan its fourth gold of this year’s Asian Games and was Lin’s first international title since moving up to the 60kg weight class following her gold-medal triumph at the 2024 Paris Olympics. Lin had taken bronze at April’s Asian Boxing Elite Boxing Championships in Ulan Batar, Mongolia, before winning silver at the World Boxing Cup in Guiyang, China, in June. Taiwan’s Hung Jiun-yi, left, in action during the men’s under-80kg semi-final against Kazakhstan’s Batyrkhan Toleugali at the Asian Games in Japan yesterday. Photo: Andy Chua, Reuters In the event in Guiyang, Lin defeated former world champion Yang by a 4-1 split decision in the semifinals to reach her first World Boxing Cup final in the heavier division. In the final, Lin was edged by Viktoriya Grafeyeva of Kazakhstan 3-2, but she avenged that defeat in the first round of the Asian Games competition with a 3-2 victory over the Kazakh boxer. Lin said before the Asian Games that she had considered retiring after winning gold at the Paris Olympics, but wanted to carry on fighting in part to defy those who questioned her eligibility following a gender row that involved US President Donald Trump, Elon Musk and author J.K. Rowling. Gold medalist Parveen Hooda of India, second left, flanked by silver medalist Chen Nien-chin of Taiwan, left, and bronze medalists Hwang Hyo Sun of North Korea, right, and Li Shu of China, second right, are pictured during the medal ceremony for the women’s 65kg boxing event at the Asian Games in Nishio, Japan, yesterday. Photo: AP She said after her victory in Nagoya that she had been “waiting for that moment when the light breaks through.” “It was really not easy at all,” she said. “It’s rare to finally reach that point where you see the dawn, and I’m just so grateful to myself for making it through,” she added. South Korea and Taiwan compete in the League of Legends e-sports finals at the Aichi Sky Expo at the Asian Games in Tokoname, Japan, yesterday. Photo: AFP Winning at the Asian Games was different from her Olympic victory, Lin said, adding that its “significance is monumental.” “I basically just felt like packing up my things and rushing back home — that was the kind of mindset I had,” she said of her previous experience. “I didn’t hold on to any hope anymore. A spokesperson for Beijing’s commerce ministry said China’s domestic industry had requested the investigation into whether imports from the […]
items.body_text:
China launches anti-dumping probe into EU chemical imports ahead of trade talks
Beijing is investigating into whether low-priced EU imports of p-nitrotoluene—a chemical used in dyes, pharmaceuticals, and pesticides—are flooding the Chinese market.
China’s commerce ministry launched an anti-dumping investigation into imports of a widely used production chemical from the European Union on Saturday, less than a week before the bloc’s trade chief was due in Beijing for talks.
A spokesperson for Beijing’s commerce ministry said China’s domestic industry had requested the investigation into whether imports from the EU of low-priced p-nitrotoluene were flooding the Chinese market, complaining of “damage to production and operations”.
The chemical is used in the production of dyes, pharmaceuticals, and pesticides.
Simmering trade tensions between Beijing and Brussels have threatened to become a full-blown trade war as the 27-nation bloc scrambles to defend its industries against a flood of Chinese exports critics argue are supported by vast subsidies.
Beijing rejects that its manufacturers’ competitiveness is based on state support and has threatened countermeasures against EU moves to block its firms.
Maros Sefcovic, the EU’s trade commissioner, and Chinese commerce minister Wang Wentao will hold critical talks on Thursday aimed at avoiding an escalation of tit-for-tat trade measures.
In September, the EU began an investigation into polyvinyl chloride imports from countries including China.
China’s newly launched investigation will conclude within 12 months, with the possibility of a six-month extension, the ministry said.
“China has repeatedly reiterated that the EU needs to face its own economic and trade problems directly and resolve mutual concerns through dialogue and consultation,” the spokesperson added.

Hotstone Yoga’s Instagram and Facebook pages were not working when […]
items.body_text:
Hong Kong’s consumer watchdog has received 286 complaints over the abrupt closure of yoga chain Hotstone Yoga, which shut its doors on Thursday.
The Consumer Council said on Friday that the complaints involved around HK$3.9 million, adding that the Customs department was investigating the case.
Hotstone Yoga’s Instagram and Facebook pages were not working when HKFP checked on Friday.
According to its website, the yoga chain has branches in Central, Causeway Bay, Jordan, Kwun Tong, Tsuen Wan, and Sha Tin.
A companies database states that Hotstone Yoga Limited was established in 2016. Its first branch opened in Kwun Tong, followed by Tsuen Wan.
The yoga studio specialises in hot yoga, a type of yoga in which students practice in heated rooms for stimulated blood flow. The chain promotes itself as the first in Hong Kong to offer hot stone yoga.
A notice posted outside the Kwun Tong branch when reporters visited on Thursday stated that due to “business operations and other actual circumstances, [Hotstone Yoga] has decided to cease operations after careful consideration.”
The notice was signed off by a law firm that said it had been appointed by the yoga company.
“After ceasing operations, Hotstone will not offer any classes, treatment, packages or other services,” it stated in Chinese.
Staff will be paid their September salaries as usual, the notice said, adding that staff can enquire with “relevant government departments” regarding employees’ rights.
Local media reported that a “victims’ group” consisting of students who had unused lessons at Hotstone Yoga had around 500 members.
Some said the company’s staff were still selling classes ahead of the closure, raising questions about potential fraud.
One woman said she spent around HK$11,800 in July on a package of 60 lessons with three free bonus sessions, leaving her with 44 unused classes.
Another said she still had 19 classes to go, valued at around HK$5,000.
A cleaner at one of the yoga studios told a customer that she was aware of the closure beforehand, but had been ordered not to reveal the news, according to Ming Pao.

items.title: Greenpeace urges HK gov’t to cut Po Pin Chau visitor quota after Nat. Day overcrowding
items.summary: Environmental NGO Greenpeace has urged the government to review its ecotourism policies and reduce visitor quotas for a popular Sai Kung trail after finding overcrowding and damage on the first day of the Golden Week holiday. The green group said in a statement that Sai Kung’s Po Pin Chau trail saw overcrowding on Thursday, which […]
items.body_text:
Environmental NGO Greenpeace has urged the government to review its ecotourism policies and reduce visitor quotas for a popular Sai Kung trail after finding overcrowding and damage on the first day of the Golden Week holiday.
The green group said in a statement that Sai Kung’s Po Pin Chau trail saw overcrowding on Thursday, which marked China’s National Day and the beginning of a weeklong holiday for the mainland.
This comes in spite of a recently established reservation system for the hiking hotspot.
Crowds caused erosion along the trail, the NGO said, with plants trampled underfoot and rampant littering in the form of plastic bottles, tissues, and food remains. Some tourists were suspected of defecating on the natural beauty site, the group added.
Hong Kong’s Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department (AFCD), which looks after the territory’s country parks, introduced a real-name booking system for the trail last month to curb overtourism.
Under the scheme, visitors planning to visit between 9am and 5pm on weekends and public holidays from September through October 7 must book in advance, with entry capped at 2,000 visitors per day.
Authorities earlier announced that some days of the National Day Golden Week holiday were already fully booked.
The AFCD said on Facebook that around 1,160 people visited the Po Pin Chau trail on Thursday, and the overall situation was “generally smooth and well-ordered.”
However, Greenpeace staff inspected the site at 8am on Thursday and found that many tourists rushed up the mountain before 9am to beat the restriction.
“Some ignored safety warnings and climbed over fences to take photos, creating dangerous situations,” Greenpeace said in a Chinese-language statement. “Some took shortcuts off the main trail for convenience, trampling and damaging adjacent vegetation, and some visitors were even found defecating by a cliffside beach, raising serious hygiene concerns.”
At around noon on Thursday, the NGO counted 64 people on the Po Pin Chau viewing platform, which was designed for only 25 people.
HKFP has reached out to the AFCD for comment.
‘Conservation-first ecotourism policy’
Greenpeace has urged the government to reduce the current daily limit of 2,000 reservations for the Po Pin Chau trail, and to consider temporarily closing down damaged sections of the site or even seasonal closures to let the area recover.
The group said authorities should adopt “a conservation-first ecotourism policy.”
“This should include carrying-capacity studies on ecologically sensitive areas across Hong Kong to formulate corresponding management measures and ensure truly sustainable ecotourism,” the Greenpeace statement stated.

Hong Kong public universities’ non-local fees jump by up to 26% as quota expands
HKU medicine, dentistry fees more than double to HK$590,000, with online users on RedNote saying hikes are ‘going too far’
Hong Kong public universities will raise undergraduate tuition fees for non-local students by up to 26 per cent in the 2027-28 academic year, marking the sharpest increase in recent years as institutions adjust to an expanded quota.
Non-local students admitted to the University of Hong Kong’s (HKU) medicine and dentistry programmes will face the steepest jump, with annual tuition rising by 137 per cent to HK$590,000 (US$75,187) to recover the high costs of clinical training.
Seven of the eight public universities have published their 2027-28 non-local tuition fees, with the average increase standing at 17 per cent compared with the current academic year.
The cumulative hike for 2027-28 represents a 41 per cent rise since 2023-24, when the non-local quota stood at 20 per cent of local places.

items.body_text:
江蕙出手了！彭佳慧第5度攻蛋 台語天后助攻發聲
〔記者陽昕翰／台北報導〕鐵肺歌后彭佳慧今晚第五度攻蛋，在台北小巨蛋舉辦「數著時間的日子巡迴演唱會」，適逢出道30週年，收到多位天王天后送上花籃祝賀，就連台語天后二姐江蕙也送花，讓她又驚喜又感動。
彭佳慧今晚第五度攻蛋，收到多位天王天后送上花籃祝賀。（記者胡舜翔攝）
彭佳慧第五度站上小巨蛋，經紀人左光平受訪透露，她這次開唱保持平常心，終於有一次開演唱會能吃到45公斤。今晚彭佳慧的兒子、女兒都到場力挺，她也傳了訊息邀請前經紀人小恬，可惜對方時間無法配合，這次沒辦法到場。
今晚包括曾國城、林美秀、羅文裕、黃中平、畢書盡、民雄等人到場力挺，江蕙、張信哲、楊乃文、戴佩妮、艾怡良、許富凱等好友也送上花籃祝福。
彭佳慧今晚第五度攻蛋，收到多位天王天后送上花籃祝賀。（記者胡舜翔攝）
其中江蕙送上花籃並寫下：「30週年，今天過後期待下一60+。」收到二姐花籃與祝福，彭佳慧感動表示：「收到二姐的花和祝福，非常驚喜，也謝謝偶像的祝福！」
彭佳慧今晚第五度攻蛋，收到多位天王天后送上花籃祝賀。（記者胡舜翔攝）
Ella也送上祝福：「親愛的姐，我們的麟洛之光，請繼續在台上發光歌唱，讓所有喜愛妳的人，可以沉浸沐浴在妳的聲音裡，愛妳，演出順利。」

items.body_text:
稱北韓成功試射AI飛彈 金與正大酸日韓「追蹤能力低下」
北韓領導人金正恩的胞妹金與正（右）稱，北韓今日試射的是一枚導入AI技術的中程戰略飛彈。（法新社檔案照）
北韓今（3日）清晨朝日本海發射一枚彈道飛彈，引起日本與南韓警戒。北韓領導人金正恩的胞妹金與正事後指出，北韓試射的是一枚導入人工智慧（AI）技術的中程戰略飛彈，又嘲諷日本與南韓在追蹤飛彈方面的能力十分有限。
《路透》報導，金與正在聲明中表示，在領導人金正恩的親自督導之下，北韓的「執行專屬特殊任務的火力分隊」執行了一次演習，朝該國東部海岸發射一枚中程飛彈。
金與正還引述了南韓與日本發布的飛彈飛行距離聲明，聲稱內容暴露出日韓兩國在追蹤飛彈方面的能力相當有限，「每當我們採取波浪式彈道模式發射飛彈時，敵方就無法從第一個彈躍點追蹤目標。」
金與正還強調，日本與南韓都「應該正視飛彈的速度」，且北韓還對飛彈導入了人工智慧技術，讓飛彈能在低空飛行時改變軌跡，「也就是說，這代表沒有方法可以避開這種攻擊。」

items.body_text:
North Korea fired a ballistic missile toward the East Sea (Sea of Japan) on Saturday, according to South Korean and Japanese authorities.
A ballistic missile launched from the Wonsan area of North Korea toward the East Sea was detected at around 6:30 a.m. on Saturday, South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) said in a notice, adding that it flew around 700 kilometers.
Seoul and Washington are “conducting a detailed analysis to determine the missile’s exact specifications,” according to the JCS. The two sides “have been tracking and sharing information on related developments since the initial stages of the launch.”

items.body_text:
North Korea’s military corruption probe is sweeping through army political departments in 2026, months after the regime exposed a major graft case in July. That case involved Pak Hui Chol, a former deputy director at the Korean People’s Army General Political Bureau. Inspections and reassignments now reach political officers across the ranks and tension inside the armed forces is rising as a result.
Senior political officers at the 8th Corps headquarters in Yomju county, North Pyongan province, have faced scrutiny since early September, a source told Daily NK on Thursday. The measures include inspections, transfers to new posts and early discharge orders, and political officers in the corps’ subordinate divisions, brigades and battalions face the same treatment.
The General Political Bureau is the Workers’ Party of Korea’s arm inside the military, overseeing ideological education, party organization and the appointment of political officers in every unit. Its political departments at each level of the army hold considerable sway over promotions and discipline.
“Since the Pak Hui Chol case, there’s a much stronger push in the military to take a fresh look at the officer ranks,” the source said. “The political department track is taking the most visible hit of all. Those officers held their posts fairly securely on the strength of family background and political credentials, and they wielded considerable authority.”
Kim Jong Un attended a rare joint meeting of party, government and military officials in Pyongyang on July 10. There, authorities exposed Pak for taking large bribes and embezzling funds during his four years in office and announced his punishment at the same gathering. The Rodong Sinmun reported on the case the following day.
Since then, military inspectors have zeroed in on corruption and misconduct rooted in personal connections. Political departments stand at the center of the resulting punishments and personnel actions, the source explained.
Officers from key sections of political departments, such as the organization and cadre affairs sections, have landed in less influential roles. Some received early discharge orders even though they had not yet reached their regular discharge date.
“As soon as word gets out that someone at the corps political department is under inspection, another officer at a division or brigade gets called in,” the source said. “Then the inspectors move down and start questioning battalion-level officers as well. Once a round of personnel reviews begins, reassignments follow one after another like a chain reaction.”
Military corruption probe exposes tangled patronage networks
The inspections have also uncovered complex webs of personal connections inside the military, with inspectors discovering that many appointments of officers were secured through favors and personal requests.
“People in the military are saying relationships between officers are far more tangled than anyone imagined,” the source said. “Talk keeps pouring out about who got their post at whose request and who has whose backing. People are becoming more aware of how widespread solicited appointments have become.”
Many within the armed forces see the campaign as part of a broader effort to root out military corruption, not a one-off inspection.
“The inspections focus on corruption, so people are asking how many officers could honestly claim to be completely free of it,” the source said. “Right now it’s concentrated on political departments, but nobody knows where the sparks will land next. Officers are keeping their heads down because no one knows which department it will spread to.”
The tension also extends beyond the military, according to the source, who referred to Kim Jong Un by the honorific title “the Marshal.”

items.title: Foreign language files land three North Korean youth league officials in custody
items.summary: North Korean authorities have arrested three youth league officials in Pyongyang over unauthorized foreign materials on their computers. The case opens a new front in the regime’s 2026 crackdown on outside information, which now reaches the cadres tasked with policing young people. The three officials worked for the Pyongyang branch of the Socialist Patriotic Youth […]
items.body_text:
North Korean authorities have arrested three youth league officials in Pyongyang over unauthorized foreign materials on their computers. The case opens a new front in the regime’s 2026 crackdown on outside information, which now reaches the cadres tasked with policing young people.
The three officials worked for the Pyongyang branch of the Socialist Patriotic Youth League, which is the Workers’ Party of Korea’s mass organization for young people between the ages of 14 and 30. The organization oversees the ideological education of North Korean youth and serves as a key pipeline into party membership.
“On Sept. 20, an anti-socialist inspection group carried out a surprise check of computers used by city youth league officials,” a source in Pyongyang told Daily NK on Thursday. “They found many foreign technical documents and books that the state had never approved for use. There were also foreign language study materials that copied South Korean and Chinese writing conventions and expressions. Three officials from the city youth league were arrested as a result.”
Anti-socialist inspection groups are joint task forces drawing on party, police and prosecution personnel. The regime dispatches them to root out what it calls anti-socialist behavior, often with no advance notice.
The inspectors showed up without warning at the officials’ workplace and went straight through their computers, according to the source. They singled out unapproved foreign technical documents and books that the officials had saved as image files.
The computers also held a range of technical standards along with explanatory materials on international law, and some of these files had been encrypted or tucked away in hidden folders on the machines. That effort at concealment made the case look even more serious to the inspectors, the source said.
What alarmed the inspectors most were the language study materials modeled on South Korean and Chinese spelling and phrasing. They labeled the files “anti-socialist cultural material” and claimed that keeping them violated the Reactionary Ideology and Culture Rejection Law.
North Korea enacted that law in December 2020 to stamp out foreign media and culture, particularly from South Korea. Its penalties include long terms in labor camps and, in the most serious cases, the death penalty.
Youth league officials arrested in broad daylight
“The inspection group arrested the three youth league officials on the spot,” the source said. “They tied their hands with rope and led them away in broad daylight. Other officials who watched it happen were shocked, and atmosphere in the whole office became extremely tense.”
Youth league officials are expected to educate young people and set an example for them to follow, which makes the discovery especially damaging for the organization and for those who supervise it.
Concern is now growing that their superiors will face collective responsibility and punishment as well, the source said, adding that many officials also fear that further inspections will soon follow across the league.
The inspection followed a recent directive from the party’s Central Committee on people with prior convictions that ordered tighter monitoring of anyone punished under the Reactionary Ideology and Culture Rejection Law or the Youth Education Guarantee Law.
Pyongyang adopted the youth education law in 2021 to police the speech, dress and thinking of young North Koreans with a view to shield them from foreign influences, especially South Korean culture and slang.

items.title: Pyongsong orders young singles to resettle in North Korean farm villages
items.summary: North Korean authorities in Pyongsong have ordered workplaces to pick unmarried young people under 30 for permanent rural placement in 2026. The forced rural relocation order has stirred deep anxiety across the South Pyongan province city, with families of those named on the lists call it a “modern-day exile.” The Pyongsong city party committee handed […]
items.body_text:
North Korean authorities in Pyongsong have ordered workplaces to pick unmarried young people under 30 for permanent rural placement in 2026. The forced rural relocation order has stirred deep anxiety across the South Pyongan province city, with families of those named on the lists call it a “modern-day exile.”
The Pyongsong city party committee handed down the order on Sept. 18, a source in South Pyongan province told Daily NK on Thursday, adding that it went to party committees at every institution and enterprise in the city. The directive called for unmarried men and women under 30 to staff schools, clinics and cultural facilities in rural areas.
That morning, the city party committee urgently summoned senior officials and personnel managers from each workplace, and officials handed over the written order and explained the selection criteria and required numbers. They also personally distributed a schedule for special lectures meant to prepare the recruits.
Pyongsong is the provincial capital of South Pyongan province, about 30 kilometers northeast of Pyongyang. The city serves as a major regional hub for wholesale trade and transportation. Its city party committee, the local arm of the Workers’ Party of Korea, controls workplaces and officials across the city.
According to the order, recruits will be spread across schools and other educational facilities in rural counties and villages. Others will go to village clinics and public health facilities or to cultural centers and similar service sites. The rest will take up posts in environmental protection work in the province.
The city party committee stressed that the order does not call for short-term labor support and targets unmarried people under 30 who can move to the assigned areas and settle there for good. Self-declared volunteers and young newlywed couples recommended by their workplaces may also be included, the order added.
North Korea has long praised young people who “volunteer” for hardship posts on farms, in coal mines and at remote construction sites. State media frequently celebrates these pledges as acts of patriotism and loyalty to the party. Defectors and sources inside the country say workplaces and party bodies often pressure young people into signing up.
The order sets a quota of about 70 people for the city as a whole. Before moving, those selected must finish short lectures run by the city party committee. The lectures aim to strengthen their ideological resolve and give them practical skills for rural life.
After the lectures, three local bodies will jointly handle the rest of the process, including the city party committee, the city people’s committee and the city social security department. Together they will confirm destinations, transfer residence registrations, assign homes and move each recruit’s belongings.
The people’s committee functions as North Korea’s local government at the city level. The social security department is the city branch of the Ministry of Social Security, which runs the country’s police force.
Forced rural relocation spreads anxiety in Pyongsong workplaces
Severe unease has spread through institutions and enterprises across Pyongsong since the order arrived. Authorities are enforcing the directive in a semi-compulsory way, so disputes over who makes the list are intensifying. Signs of irregularities in the selection process are also growing more pronounced.
The order requires young people to leave the city where they grew up for good and settle in remote farming villages where they have no family ties and few resources. Young candidates and their families are now searching for any way to get their names off the list.
Many of them describe the assignment as “a modern-day exile,” according to the source. items.title: Verstappen claims pole at Grand Prix in Malaysia
items.summary: Max Verstappen delivered a sublime lap in his Red Bull to qualify fastest for Sunday's Formula 1 Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.
items.body_text:
Red Bull's Max Verstappen claimed his first pole position of the season at the Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia on Saturday, with Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton joining him on the front row.
It is the first time two great rivals have shared the front row of the grid since the Hungarian Grand Prix in 2023.
Verstappen's teammate, Isack Hadjar, was third fastest but will start eighth due to a grid penalty, with championship leader Kimi Antonelli in third alongside Ferrari's Charles Leclerc.
Oscar Piastri was pipped to sixth by his teammate Lando Norris, but will move up a position as a result of Hadjar's penalty to start sixth as McLaren locked out the third row of the grid.
George Russell, who so spectacularly won the last Grand Prix in Azerbaijan last week, will start seventh in what was an alarming performance for Mercedes, who came to Malaysia with a big upgrade package.
"It's very difficult to understand," Mercedes boss Toto Wolff told Sky Sports.
"We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we didn't see all year.
"But then you can say it's very hot, with the tarmac very different to all the tracks.
"[We] looked really good in the morning; we seemed to have, at least with Kimi [Antonelli], made a step in understanding. And then in qualifying, it was a little bit back to what we saw before — just no performance."
Verstappen was the last driver to win a Grand Prix in Malaysia in 2017, in what was his second career victory, before the race was taken off the calendar after the government said it could not justify the costs.
Nine years and four championships later, the Dutchman showed he was still the man to beat in Sepang with a time of 1 minute 35.130 seconds.
"It's fantastic, we've been trying for many Grands Prix to get more, sometimes a bit closer to the others. But to finally get it from where we started the season [it's] pretty incredible," said Verstappen as he eyes his first win of the season.
Hamilton, who also has one victory in Sepang, struggled with tyre degradation in practice sessions but the veteran Briton snatched second from Hadjar in the dying stages of the final qualifying session.
"It's so hot here, I keep saying it. But that's made it a massive challenge for the tyres, for the car, for the mechanics in the garage," Hamilton said.
"We made so many changes through all these practice sessions because the cars are sliding, these tyres are overheating. It was really, really hard to find a good balance. We made one last change going into qualifying and I think we hit the sweet spot."
Hadjar had exceeded his seasonal allowance for engines, which resulted in a five-place grid penalty.
"It's a bit unfortunate we take the penalty on a track that fast," Hadjar said.
"But you know, from P8, I'm confident we can go through the field and come back for a good result."
Reuters/ABC

items.title: De Minaur fights into quarterfinals in China
items.summary: It wasn't easy, but Australian Alex de Minaur has booked his spot in the quarterfinals of the China Open with a gutsy win over France's Quentin Halys.
items.body_text:
Alex de Minaur has been pushed to the limit, before breaking the resistance of French qualifier Quentin Halys and advancing to his second consecutive China Open quarterfinal.
The Australian, who has had a seesawing second half of the year, lost the first set in Beijing on Saturday, before grinding his way back into the match.
After winning the first set 6-3, world number 50 Halys opened up a 5-3 lead in the second and was serving for the match, before de Minaur rallied to break back, then clinch a neck-and-neck tie break 7-5 to set up a decider.
The third set was another close affair, before de Minaur was able to break at 5-5 and secure a hard-fought 3-6 7-6 (5) 7-5 win in 2 hours 47 minutes.
Victory evened up their head-to-head record at 2-2 and put de Minaur into the quarters, where the world number 10 will play Andrey Rublev, currently ranked number 20 in the world, but a former top-10 player himself.
Rublev was also pushed to the limit before beating fellow Russian Roman Safiullin 6-2 3-6 6-4.
De Minaur will be looking to repeat or better last year's performance at the ATP 500 event, when he made the semifinals before losing to then world number 1 Jannik Sinner.
It has been an up-and-down year for de Minaur, who started 2026 off well by reaching the last eight at the Australian Open.
He continued that momentum into February, when he won the ATP 500 event in Rotterdam.
De Minaur followed that by reaching the French Open's third round and the fourth round at Wimbledon, before disappointingly bowing out in the second round of the US Open in September.
However, he bounced back impressively by steering Australia to victory over Poland in their Davis Cup clash in Brisbane, before beating in-from German Alexander Zverev at the Laver Cup in London.
Zverev, who has won two majors this year — at Roland Garros in June and Flushing Meadows in September — is top seed in Beijing and was scheduled to play China's Juncheng Shang later on Saturday.
AAP

items.title: David Fifita leads Australia in wild mismatch against PNG
items.summary: Australia and captain David Fifita have routed Papua New Guinea in the annual Prime Minister's XIII game in Port Moresby, while winger Jada Taylor has put her hand up for a World Cup berth after the women's team handed PNG a record loss.
items.body_text:
Fri, 11 Sept, 7:50 pm, Final score, Rabbitohs 10, Knights 20
Prime Minister's XIIIs thrash PNG in 11- and 12-try victories in Port Moresby
A rag-tag Australian side has outclassed Papua New Guinea 60-10 in the annual Prime Minister's XIII clash in Port Moresby.
The Australians scored 11 tries and exposed the PNG side's defensive frailties almost at will in what was the 20th men's Prime Minister's XIII match.
It was hardly a conventional game at the National Football Stadium on Saturday, with Australia switching on and off as players became accustomed to their makeshift position.
Ezra Mam spent time at fullback. Jock Madden appeared to be playing on an edge. Jamal Fogarty stood in the centres, and Josh Curran kicked a goal.
At one stage they had three regular hookers on the field.
In one piece of consistency, captain David Fifita started and finished the match as a devastating left centre.
Commentator Cooper Cronk mused it was coach Ben Teo's way of keeping the Aussies engaged after a long, hard season.
It was at times chaotic and they dropped the ball a lot, but it was fun. Less so for the PNG side, who were not just outclassed but also ill-disciplined, missing 47 tackles — 28 in the first half alone.
With the PNG Chiefs' arrival in the NRL fast approaching, it is clear the next level of local players are still a long way from that standard.
On a positive note, earlier on Saturday the Junior Kumuls scored a historic first win over the Australian Schoolboys, 18-10.
If Kangaroos coach Kevin Walters hasn't settled on his squad for this month's Rugby League World Cup, several players put their hands up.
Regular back-rower Fifita, who showed his class and power in the centres on Saturday, first appeared in the PM's XIII game seven years ago and looked destined for higher honours that never arrived. Maybe that time is approaching again.
Mam and fellow half Lachlan Galvin showed more than one glimpse of their brilliance, while hulking front-rower Tom Hazelton was one of the best players on the field.
For former NRL and current London Broncos coach Jason Demetriou, who will guide the PNG Kumuls at the World Cup, there was not a lot to love.
Sylvester Namo should be there, while uncapped centre Stanford Talita and fullback Sanny Wabo were dangerous at times and could find their way into Demetriou's squad.
In the women's game, Australia was also successful, dishing out a 66-6 thumping of their hosts.
PNG might have scored for the first time in three years, but Australia was a class above, crossing for 12 tries to one to rack up the biggest winning margin in the fixture's history.
While the standard of PNG's second-tier players has improved alongside the growth of the national women's competition, the Santos Cup, so too has that of the Australians.
Several showed they would not be out of place if called up to coach Jess Skinner's Jillaroos for this month's 2026 Rugby League World Cup.
Jada Taylor scored three tries and was almost impossible to handle at times, showing her versatility by playing on the wing, despite playing her club football at fullback.
Half Kasey Reh, centre Tahlia O'Brien, hooker Taneka Todhunter and back-rower Tayla Preston were others who impressed in what was effectively an audition in front of Skinner for a grander stage.
PNG Orchids coach Craig Sandercock, who this year guided Wests Tigers to their first NRLW finals series, would also have enjoyed the opportunity to see the next generation of PNG players.
There was no doubt they were outclassed, and they struggled for time with the ball, having just 37 per cent possession.
However, they had an 85 per cent completion rate and tried hard in defence, before tiring late in each half.
AAP

items.body_text:
Ten people injured, P-plater charged after car crashes into Newcastle Knights fans
Updated ,first published
A five-year-old girl was left fighting for her life and nine others were injured when a teenage P-plate driver allegedly lost control of his car and careered into jubilant crowds lining a Newcastle street to wave the Knights off to the NRL grand final.
One of the injured, Chris Clancy, said the car appeared to speed up as it went through a roundabout, and then lost control on the wet road. “No-one had time to move,” he said. “I thought I was going to die, it happened so fast.”
Fans at the crash site rushed to provide first aid as emergency crews rushed to the scene and word of the collision spread through the tens of thousands of excited fans waiting for a glimpse of their team. The team’s bus, which had not yet departed when the crash occurred, was rerouted, and players were informed.
“They were shocked, it was a very sombre bus ride,” said one of those aboard. “Our fans mean everything to us. For that to happen; horrible.”
The five-year-old girl was in a critical condition in John Hunter Hospital on Saturday evening. One patient was in a serious but stable condition, and five were stable. Three had been discharged.
Police arrested the 18-year-old driver, Indika Bambrick Samarasinghe, at the crash site and took him for mandatory drug and alcohol testing. He was later charged with three counts each of dangerous driving occasioning grievous bodily harm, negligent driving occasioning grievous bodily harm and causing bodily harm by misconduct in charge of a motor vehicle. He was refused police bail to face a court on Sunday.
NSW Police Assistant Commissioner David Waddell said officers were investigating reports the P-plater had been “driving erratically” before he lost control of the vehicle.
Footage posted to social media depicted the BMW careering around the roundabout moments before the crash, as shocked onlookers were heard screaming. The driver is expected to be charged, but no charges had been laid at the time of publication.
Onlookers expressed anger towards the occupants of the car after the crash, police said. “We had to get the three of them out of there because the crowd did turn on them,” Waddell said.
Witness Dean Liddell said he could hear the vehicle coming towards the crowd and then “all hell broke loose”.
“I watched the little girl get dragged underneath the car. Seeing the whole scene unfold, it took me 10 minutes until I could say anything to anyone,” Liddell said.
He said the crowd grabbed the driver from the wreck and a scuffle began before police intervened.
“If the copper wasn’t there the driver would have had massive injuries as well,” he said.
The accident came after a joyous week in Newcastle, where the city threw its support behind a team that has not won a premiership for 25 years. The Knights had been expected to be inspired by the joy of their supporters during the grand final, but will now also feel the weight of the tragedy when they take the field.
Newcastle Knights captain Kalyn Ponga said on social media that players “hearts are with everyone affected” by the crash. “We’re thinking of you, your families and everyone in our Newcastle community.”
Longtime league watchers say no other grand final has been played under such a shadow.
“It’s heartbreaking for the whole rugby league community, not just in Newcastle,” said Brad Fittler, a former Roosters captain and a member of the league hall of fame. “We’ve never seen anything like this ahead of a grand final and it puts everything in perspective.”
Australian Rugby League Commission executive chairman Peter V’Landys said he was deeply saddened by the crash. When asked whether it would affect plans for Sunday night’s game, he said “we’re just concerned about the victims at the moment.”

items.body_text:
Ten people have been injured, one critically, after a car crashed into a crowd of people in Newcastle waiting to farewell the Knights team bus before the NRL grand final.
New South Wales police said a five-year-old girl remained in a critical condition after the crash on Saturday morning.
Initially a 67-year-old man was also in a critical. The man is now in a serious but stable condition.
John Hunter hospital provided an update to Australian Associated Press on Saturday night confirming five other patients were in a stable condition and three others had been discharged.
The injured were treated on the scene by NSW ambulance paramedics, before being taken to hospital.
The P-plate driver was an 18-year-old man who was arrested at the scene and taken to hospital for mandatory testing, police said.
The assistant commissioner David Waddell said there were reports the man was driving erratically before losing control and careening into the crowd. It was expected he would be charged later on Saturday.
The man had two others in the car with him.
“We had to get them out of there because the crowd did turn on them,” Waddell said.
The police minister, Yasmin Catley, said so many lives had been affected by a split-second decision, as she urged other drivers to take care over the NSW long weekend.
“We have already started Saturday morning with this devastation,” she said.
“Nobody can comprehend what has happened with this terrible tragedy.”
The roads minister, Jenny Aitchison, said the incident could have been worse, with more than 1,000 people gathered in the area where it occurred.
Emergency services were called to Newcastle Link Road at the Transfield Drive roundabout in Wallsend about 9.30am on Saturday after reports a vehicle struck multiple people in a crowd.
“Several people have been injured and are currently receiving treatment at the scene,” police said.
“Police have commenced an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the incident, with initial inquiries indicating it is not believed to be terror related.”
Gavin Morris, the mayor of Newcastle, told the ABC that the driver, who he said was a Knights fan, lost control while revving his car shortly before the team arrived.
“I’ve spoken to the authorities, a number of which, and look, first of all, it is under investigation, and the young driver is now with police, so it appears that he was revving the car in some form. He was excited. He was a supporter. He was, you know, a fan,” Morris said.
“It appears that he’s lost control of the car, and he’s gone … sideways into the crowd.”
Footage posted on social media appeared to show the car being driven quickly around a roundabout shortly before the crash.
Other images showed it had careened off the road soon afterwards.
A witness to the incident, Dylan Prior told ABC News that the car was “revving a bit” before it ran into a group of people.
“I saw some young kids go flying, and people running to help the victims,” he said.
“Everyone was yelling and hysterical, yelling at the driver.
“They were screaming for help.”
The Newcastle Link Road was closed in both directions, leading to the diversion of the Knights grand final procession.
The club confirmed in an Instagram post that it had changed its route, apologising to fans who may have missed farewelling the team but saying “public safety is our priority”.
Police appealed for fans to leave the area.
“Police acknowledge many loyal supporters may have missed the opportunity to see the team and show their support.
“Members of the public are asked to safely disperse from the area and keep roadways clear to assist emergency services and traffic management efforts.
“Police thank the community for their patience, cooperation and assistance.”
The NSW premier, Chris Minns, said his thoughts were with the families and friends of those injured.
“It’s heartbreaking to see fans who were sending off their grand final team involved in such a terrible incident,” he said.

items.title: One Nation vows to abolish First Nations treaty and legalise pepper spray at Victorian campaign launch
items.summary: Candidate Mark Nicholson said former premiers Daniel Andrews and Jacinta Allan would be ‘in prison by Christmas’ if One Nation won the electionGet our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcastOne Nation has launched its Victorian election campaign, vowing to legalise the personal use of pepper spray, abolish the state’s treaty with Indigenous people, and scrap payroll tax in regional Victoria.A social media post announcing its policy to “make it cheaper and easier to set up new busines
items.body_text:
One Nation has launched its Victorian election campaign, vowing to legalise the personal use of pepper spray, abolish the state’s treaty with Indigenous people, and scrap payroll tax in regional Victoria.
A social media post announcing its policy to “make it cheaper and easier to set up new businesses in Victoria” featured an AI-generated image of a “taaditional [sic] fish n’chips” shop.
One Nation used its official campaign launch at Crown Casino to unveil candidates for the state’s upper house and all 88 lower house electorates.
These candidates include a former Liberal who has won support from alleged underworld figures, a naturopath who has endorsed Donald Trump’s unfounded claim that paracetamol is linked to autism and a former shire councillor who lost his licence for drink-driving.
The party is understood to have again prevented reporters from certain media outlets from attending the launch. It has previously barred the ABC, Guardian, and the Age from its media events. The Guardian did not attempt to attend Saturday’s launch.
The Herald Sun reported that Northern Metropolitan candidate and creator of the party’s Please Explain Cartoon, Mark Nicholson, vowed at the launch that if One Nation won the election, former premiers Daniel Andrews and Jacinta Allan would be “in prison by Christmas”.
Details of other policies were scant online, but a 63-page document was reportedly circulated at the event that included plans to “gang up on gangs”.
Images of the document show it was described as One Nation’s policy platform and “The Real Deal for Victoria”, with a focus on restoring safety, prosperity and trust.
According to the party’s website on Saturday afternoon, an “update [was] in progress” regarding its crime policy.
The party’s Victorian state president, Warren Pickering, told radio 3AW Melbourne on Friday that crime and bail remained a top priority for One Nation.
“[It] is the key issue in the state right now and people need to feel safe in their homes and places of work once more,” he said.
“You make that happen by taking a pragmatic approach, not an expensive one, to ensuring we get more police on the streets, get our empty stations manned and ensure bail laws and sentences are fitting with the crimes.”
The party claimed in social media posts that more than 1,000 people attended the launch, but other estimates put the crowd at several hundred lower than that. A smaller group of protesters outside were monitored by police.
The party has come under fire for practices that could see it collect as much as $633,000 from people who have nominated for the Victorian election, with some potential candidates questioning whether the party is staging a “cash grab”.
While the party has fashioned itself as representing the working class, its founder Pauline Hanson has faced a series of revelations about her links to billionaire Gina Rinehart, including exclusive use of a private jet, and staying at her multimillion-dollar homes.
– Additional reporting by Australian Associated Press

items.body_text:
A severe weather system continues to dump heavy rain into sodden riverine catchments across Victoria, sparking widespread warnings of transport disruption and delays.
The Bureau of Meteorology has issued a flood watch for most of Victoria including the north-east, central, south-west and north-west, as well as parts of Gippsland.
It also said bursts of heavy rain accompanied by potentially damaging winds and thunderstorms were possible in parts of New South Wales as a band of heavy weather swept the southern states.
In Victoria, the Otway Ranges, south-west of Melbourne, and Gippsland are facing 24-hour rain totals up to 90mm, with isolated falls up to 150mm possible in elevated regions.
Six-hourly totals up to 70mm have been forecast, with conditions not expected to ease until late Saturday.
Gippsland is also likely to be hard hit, with 24-hour totals between 50 and 80mm likely and isolated falls up to 110mm possible, with conditions easing Sunday morning.
“This is on top of the rain you’ve already had in the last few days, so I’ll say it again, the soils are already saturated,” senior meteorologist Angus Hines said.
Over 100mm has already fallen in parts of the Otways, with heavy rain continuing to fall on Saturday afternoon.
“Another 30 to 50mm on top of last night’s deluge could certainly fall there,” Hines said.
The rain was centred around a low pressure system situated over the Murray River on the NSW-Victorian border.
For now, there was just one official flood warning in place for the Bunyip River in Victoria but Hines said more rivers were likely to see rises across the weekend.
He said the situation was dynamic and it was highly likely more flood warnings would be issued.
In NSW, a severe thunderstorm warning has been issued for the Illawarra and parts of south coast, central and southern tablelands, the central west slopes and plains.
Locations which may be affected include Orange, Goulburn, Dubbo, Nowra, Bowral and Bathurst.
The severe weather is expected to clear by the end of the weekend.

items.title: G7 nations agree to release 100 million barrels of oil, including diesel, amid energy crunch
items.summary: The release would begin immediately and take four months, starting with a "substantial" diesel release within the first 20 days. Diesel prices have soared globally due to the oil supply crunch brought on by fighting in the Middle East between the U.S. and Iran.
items.body_text:
G7 nations agree to release 100 million barrels of oil, including diesel, amid energy crunch
Move would start with 'substantial' diesel release within first 20 days
The G7 nations said they agreed to release 100 million barrels of oil, starting with "substantial" amounts of diesel, after the fuel recently hit record prices in the United States.
U.S. President Donald Trump said on social media the diesel release would happen "immediately," echoing a G7 promise to start immediately with a "frontloaded substantial release" of diesel within the next 20 days and the rest over four months.
Trump and his Republican Party face pressure to address surging prices ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm elections.
The president faces lagging approval ratings as the Iran war and his trade battles have increased U.S. prices for oil and other goods.
Gas and diesel prices have soared during the eight-month-long war, a cost Trump has repeatedly said is worth it for making sure Iran does not obtain nuclear weapons. Trump has insisted prices will come down after the war, though there's no end in sight.
The average price of diesel in Canada was $2.63 per litre as of Thursday, though prices were higher in some cities, like Vancouver, where a litre of the fuel cost about $2.71. Heightened prices put pressure on transport truck drivers and farmers, who rely on diesel to run vehicles and equipment.
France holds the rotating presidency of the G7 group and made the announcement in a statement released after videoconference talks that French President Emmanuel Macron presided over. The G7 countries are Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the U.K. and the U.S., plus EU representation.
The International Energy Agency will co-ordinate the effort to combat soaring fuel prices.
"We will implement our commitments with a co-ordinated release through the IEA of 100 million barrels (MB) to begin immediately over 4 months, including a front-loaded substantial diesel release within the first 20 days by G7 members and partners," the statement said.
The release follows a March announcement that International Energy Agency member countries would release 426 million barrels of oil and products to stabilize the oil market.
The move also comes after Trump last week floated the idea of banning diesel exports in hopes of bringing down gas prices for American drivers — a move experts caution could backfire, putting strain on an already-stretched global fuel market and further raising prices globally.
But the G7 statement said the group, which includes the United States, also agreed not to limit energy exports to each other.
"We reaffirm our commitment to refrain from export restrictions on energy and energy products between G7 countries and call on all producers to refrain from imposing bans that could exacerbate market tensions," it said.
Trump had a conversation overnight with Macron about the need to address rising fuel prices and the availability of petroleum products, according to the French Embassy in the U.S., before chairing the videoconference.
A new AP-NORC poll found that a majority of U.S. adults blame Trump for higher prices, and approval on his handling of the economy hit a new low.
With files from CBC News
items.normalised_title: g7 nations agree to release 100 million barrels of oil including diesel amid energy crunch

items.title: CBS Sports describes Tony Romo's permanent exit as mutual parting
items.summary: CBS Sports and Tony Romo have officially parted ways, one month after the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback pleaded no contest to charges of operating a vehicle while intoxicated.
items.body_text:
CBS Sports describes Tony Romo's permanent exit as mutual parting
Ex-NFL QB pleaded no contest to DWI charge after July traffic stop in Wisconsin
CBS Sports and Tony Romo have officially parted ways, one month after the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback pleaded no contest to charges of operating a vehicle while intoxicated.
Romo had been on leave since his July 23 arrest in Wisconsin. He had been the lead game analyst for CBS' NFL coverage since 2017.
"CBS Sports and Tony Romo have mutually agreed to part ways," CBS Sports said Friday in a statement. "We thank Tony for his contributions over the past nine years and wish him the best moving forward."
Analyst JJ Watt had joined play-by-play announcer Jim Nantz and sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson on CBS Sports' lead NFL team during Romo's absence. Watt will continue in that role now and all other CBS teams will remain the same.
"I'm proud of what I accomplished at CBS Sports over the last nine years," Romo said in a statement. "I approached my role as a game analyst the way I've approached everything in my life, with a desire to win and be the best that I can be.
"I'm going to use this time to take a break, something I've never done before, and focus on my health and my family before moving on to my next opportunity. I am grateful for my time with CBS Sports and for the continued support of my family and friends, as well as the NFL community and fans."
Romo was arrested following a traffic stop as he was driving south on Interstate 43 in Wisconsin. He pleaded no contest to a charge of operating while intoxicated on Sept. 1 and issued a statement apologizing for the actions that led to his arrest.
According to Milwaukee County court records, Romo lost his driving privileges for six months and was ordered to complete an alcohol assessment program.
"The past month has been difficult, but it has also been personally significant," Romo said Sept. 1 in a statement on Instagram. "It has required me to confront and own my mistakes fully — to the Lord, to myself, to my family and now to the public."
Romo said the multiple back surgeries that led to his retirement as a player "left me with constant, debilitating pain." He noted that the pain "led to a dependence on pain medication, and my efforts to get off those medications led to an over-reliance on alcohol."
"None of this is an excuse," Romo said. "These are my failures and I take responsibility for them."
Romo said he is working with a team of doctors to address his health and "make the necessary changes."
The 46-year-old Romo made four Pro Bowl appearances during a playing career that ran from 2004-16 and was spent entirely with Dallas.

items.title: 'I was fighting for my life': Indian pilot hailed as hero recalls FlyDubai cockpit attack
items.summary: The Indian airline captain who helped thwart an apparent attempt to crash a FlyDubai flight described Friday how he fought for his life in the minutes after his co-pilot stabbed him and the plane began a steep descent.
items.body_text:
'I was fighting for my life': Indian pilot hailed as hero recalls FlyDubai cockpit attack
Captain Smit Machchhar spoke to Indian PM in interview broadcast live from hospital
The Indian airline captain who helped thwart an apparent attempt to crash a FlyDubai flight described Friday how he fought for his life in the minutes after his co-pilot stabbed him and the plane began a steep descent.
Captain Smit Machchhar, recovering in an Abu Dhabi hospital, told Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in a video call broadcast live on television news channels that he knew he had to get back on his feet to save the passengers aboard the aircraft.
"I had so many wounds. I had fallen down," he said from the hospital, his head bandaged and tubes in his nose, before breaking down as he recalled the attack.
"I was fighting for my life. At one point, I realized that if I didn't get up … then passengers would lose their lives," he told Modi.
- Passengers foil bid to crash Dubai-Tel Aviv flight after co-pilot stabbed pilot, Israel says
- What we know so far about the midair FlyDubai attack
Machchhar, who is from India's financial hub of Mumbai, was seriously injured in Wednesday's attack but managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers to enter and restrain the attacker as the Boeing 737 descended sharply, witnesses and Israeli authorities said.
He has been hailed as a hero for his actions, with world leaders saying he helped prevent a potential disaster.
The flight, carrying 182 people from Dubai to Tel Aviv, was diverted to Tabuk in northwestern Saudi Arabia for an emergency landing.
Machchhar said that during those difficult moments, he recited the Hanuman Chalisa, a Hindu devotional hymn dedicated to Lord Hanuman and traditionally recited as a prayer for strength and courage.
"Lord Hanuman gave me courage," he told Modi.
Machchhar, who is married and has two children, has worked for FlyDubai for about four years, according to his LinkedIn profile. Before joining the airline, he spent 11 years with SpiceJet, an Indian low-cost carrier, where he served as a senior commander and line training captain. He logged more than 9,750 flying hours with SpiceJet.
Israel to repatriate citizens in U.A.E.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the attacker, an Omani national, was arrested in Saudi Arabia and was undergoing interrogation there. His motive for the attack was not immediately clear.
Netanyahu and U.S. President Donald Trump have publicly mused about potential links between the attacker and Iran without providing any evidence to support the allegations.
Trump's suggestion that there could be an Iranian link adds a new layer of uncertainty to the on-and-off diplomatic efforts aimed at bringing an end to the seven-month Iran war.
He said Thursday if it is determined that Iranian agents were behind the attack, the United States will "hit them very hard."
Meanwhile, Israel was beginning repatriation flights on Friday to bring back passengers stranded in the United Arab Emirates after commercial travel between the two countries was suspended following the violent incident.
The Ben Gurion International Airport in Tel Aviv listed carriers Arkia and Israir with flights scheduled to arrive from Dubai late Friday and early Saturday. El Al was expected to fly passengers from Dubai to Israel on Sunday.
The first repatriation flight left the UAE shortly before 11 p.m. and landed in Tel Aviv just after 1 a.m., according to the Ben Gurion International Airport website.
Dubai has been a popular destination for Israelis since Israel and the U.A.E. established ties in 2020 as part of the Trump administration's Abraham Accords to normalize ties between Israel and Arab countries.

items.title: Flydubai co-pilot attacked with an axe, UAE says
items.summary: Investigators describe incident as attempted terror attack
items.body_text:
The co-pilot of flydubai flight FZ1073, which was bound for Israel, attempted to carry out a “terrorist attack” with an axe during the flight, the United Arab Emirates prosecutor general said on Saturday.
The co-pilot was identified as Hammam al-Hammami, an Omani national, a source with direct knowledge of the matter told Reuters. A second source briefed on the investigation confirmed the co-pilot’s name. UAE authorities did not immediately respond to a request for confirmation of his identity.
Disaster was averted on Wednesday after passengers and crew subdued the co-pilot, who had attacked the captain in what Israeli officials said was an apparent attempt to crash the plane carrying more than 170 passengers and crew.
While Emirati authorities and the airline have not publicly identified the co-pilot, Israeli officials have previously said he is an Omani national. Oman has not commented on the incident.
“Investigations into the incident involving flydubai flight FZ1073 found that the co-pilot had attempted to carry out a terrorist attack,” Prosecutor General Hamad Saif Al Shamsi said in a statement carried by the UAE’s state news agency.
The co-pilot attacked the pilot inside the cockpit with a crash axe and attempted to take control of the aircraft, the prosecutor general said.
A crash axe is typically kept in the cockpit for use during emergencies such as crashes.
The investigation into flight FZ1073, including the suspect’s motives, is ongoing, and the findings will be released once the “necessary procedures” have been completed, the prosecutor general said. The UAE is leading the investigation. The airline is owned by Dubai’s government.
Co-pilot who tried to crash FlyDubai flight was banned from flying by Oman over extremism concerns
The prosecutor general’s comments were the first by Emirati investigators to describe the incident as an attempted terrorist attack. Following the release of the prosecutor general’s statement, Anwar Gargash, a senior adviser to the UAE president, said on X that the Gulf country had zero tolerance for terrorism and would show no leniency toward extremist rhetoric.
Flydubai said the circumstances surrounding the incident were still under investigation and that it was not in a position to comment further, a spokesperson said on Saturday.
Reuters could not immediately verify professional and social media pages reportedly belonging to the co-pilot, which suggested he had worked for other airlines.
Royal Air Maroc told Reuters, in response to a question about his potential employment there in the past, that he had undergone a three-month training with the airline in 2025 but his application to work there afterwards was rejected. RAM did not elaborate.
In his first public comments on the incident, flydubai Chief Executive Ghaith al Ghaith on Friday said that the flight diverted after a “safety incident” inside the cockpit.
Most of the passengers on board were Israeli nationals.
A reserve flydubai pilot travelling on the flight took control of the aircraft and landed it at Tabuk airport in northwestern Saudi Arabia, where the co-pilot was detained by Saudi authorities.
The co-pilot was transferred from Saudi Arabia to Abu Dhabi on Thursday. A source briefed on the investigation told Reuters on Friday that Israeli officials were expected to question the co-pilot in the UAE. The source declined to say which Israeli agency or authority would take part.
An Israeli government official said that Israeli investigators would take part alongside Emirati authorities in the UAE-led investigation.
Israel does not have official diplomatic relations with Oman, and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said pilots from such countries were not permitted to operate flights to Israel. It was not clear how the co-pilot came to be assigned to the flight to Tel Aviv.

items.title: Polling shows Democrats ahead as the midterms approach, but polls cannot capture the partisanship of elections
items.summary: It’s hard to overstate how little the actual candidates matter to Americans’ voting choices
items.body_text:
There’s a lot at stake in the U.S. congressional midterm elections next month. President Donald Trump has never faced Democratic majorities in both chambers of Congress or even a Democratic-majority Senate, but polls show the party in a strong position to win at least the House of Representatives and perhaps both.
So a lot could change. Congress could actually return to oversight and reassert its authority on tariffs, war powers and spending. Impeachment hearings and a trial for Mr. Trump surely become likely, although removing him from office would require Republican senators to abandon him en masse.
With a big Democratic wave, long-term and consequential Democratic majorities become possible. After Mr. Trump’s first term, Joe Biden’s presidency showed that healthy democratic norms will not automatically return when Mr. Trump leaves office. An ambitious Democratic president in 2029 could try to fix institutional sources of democratic backsliding but would need working majorities.
With enough senators, Democrats could end the Senate filibuster, add the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico as new (heavily Democratic) states, fill future Supreme Court vacancies and reform and expand the court, pass a new Voting Rights Act and a national right to abortion access law and introduce election reforms for the House of Representatives.
Polls show a Democratic sweep as increasingly likely based on many contributing factors. In 2024, Mr. Trump did well among Hispanic voters, but they’ve soured on him. That will cost Republicans, especially in Texas and Florida. Plus, there’s the usual midterm swing against the president’s party, the unpopular Iran war, gas prices, some dreadful Republican candidates chosen by primary voters (see Texas) and Mr. Trump’s unpopularity, especially on key issues such as affordability, according to a recent Strength In Numbers/Verasight report.
Analysis: In the U.S. midterms’ murky math, economic distress is the only clear variable
Democrats need to flip only three seats to take back the House, and forecasts have them doing that handily, winning roughly 235 of the chamber’s 435 seats, with a simple majority requiring 218. It could be even more lopsided: In some states, such as Texas, gerrymanders have spread Republican voters too thinly to survive a big blue wave – another Trump-led campaign strategy that may backfire.
For a bare Senate majority of 51, Democrats need four seats held by Republicans while hanging on to the ones they currently have. Some key races (with Sept. 24 polling aggregates) are in the usual toss-up states such as Georgia (Democrat leading by eight percentage points), Maine (D +0.8), Michigan (D +2.7) and North Carolina (D +8.6), but many are reliably Republican: Alaska (D +2.6), Iowa (D +1.7), Ohio (D +4.1) and Texas (D +3.1). Even Kansas (R +0.7) and Nebraska (Ind +1.1) are conceivable Republican losses.
Polls and pollsters take a beating largely because we expect too much from them. How can we go awry when reading them? A Sept. 17-20 Ipsos poll shows the Republicans in trouble, with Mr. Trump’s approval rating at 32 per cent, which is below George W. Bush’s in 2006, when the Republicans lost six Senate seats, 31 House seats and the majority in both chambers.
But there’s a lot of uncertainty when it comes to what Trump disapprovers – including the 22 per cent of his voters who now disapprove of him − will do, according to an Economist/YouGov poll. In 2016 and 2024, non-MAGA Republicans stuck with their party and gave Mr. Trump his victories. If the election were held today, Republicans are at about 43 per cent on the “generic ballot,” indicating that many will vote Republican again.
Still, non-MAGA Republicans and Republican-leaning Independents are a big portion of the “don’t knows” regarding their 2026 choice. Very few will vote Democrat, and some will stay home or vote for a third party, but there are still unknowns and undecideds.
Polls cannot capture the fact that elections activate

items.title: Can Kemi Badenoch turn things around for the British Conservatives?
items.summary: The first Black woman to lead a U.K. major political party is hitting her stride, but the Tories have a long way to go
items.body_text:
Kemi Badenoch’s future as leader of Britain’s Conservative Party could not have looked much worse this time last year, and there were real doubts about the survival of the 200-year old party, long considered the most successful in Europe.
But in a remarkable turnaround, Ms. Badenoch has brought the Tories back into relevance and become one of the most popular politicians in the country.
Some pundits have called it a “Keminaissance.” It’s quite a feat for the 46-year old former computer engineer, who grew up in Nigeria and is the first Black woman to lead a major political party in the United Kingdom.
As she heads to the Conservative Party’s annual conference this weekend in Birmingham, Ms. Badenoch can relish the results of a recent poll by YouGov involving 17,000 adults. A seat projection based on the poll found that if an election were held that day, no party would win a majority, but the Conservatives would be second to Labour and ahead of Reform UK.
A similar poll a year ago predicted the Tories would be wiped out and Reform would win a resounding victory.
“I knew very well what she’s capable of because in her character, she’s tough, very tough,” said Tory MP Iain Duncan Smith, who led the party from 2001 to 2003.
“She reminds me a lot of the sort of determination and intellect of Margaret Thatcher,” he said, referring to the Conservative heavyweight who served as prime minister from 1979 to 1990. “She’s got a certainty about what she believes.”
Mr. Duncan Smith credited Ms. Badenoch with uniting the notoriously fractious party. “The important thing is we need to be able to let the people know there is a major choice to be made at the next election. I think Kemi epitomizes that,” he added.
Not many people gave Ms. Badenoch much of a chance when she narrowly won the race to become leader in November, 2024. The party was still reeling from a disastrous election four months earlier and Nigel Farage, Reform’s populist leader, was usurping Ms. Badenoch as the leading voice on the right.
Ms. Badenoch had only been an MP since 2017 and she lacked the posh, privately educated upbringing synonymous with Tory leaders of the past.
She was born Olukemi Olufunto Adegoke in the London borough of Wimbledon to well-off parents from Nigeria – her father was a doctor and her mother a professor of physiology. Her parents had come to Britain because Ms. Badenoch’s mother needed a specialist obstetrician. The family returned to Lagos shortly after she was born.
By the time Ms. Badenoch was a teenager, Nigeria had been rocked by years of political instability and her parents had lost most of their money. They sent their daughter to London to live with a family friend and finish high school. To make ends meet, Ms. Badenoch took a job at McDonald’s.
She no longer identifies as Nigerian. “I’m Nigerian through ancestry,” she has said, “but by identity, I’m not really.”
In another interview, she said growing up in Nigeria had given her an appreciation of Britain. “I always say that Britain is the best place in the world to be Black. And I still stick to that.”
After high school, she studied computer engineering at the University of Sussex and landed IT jobs in banking. She joined the Conservatives while at university and embraced the ideas of self-reliance, free enterprise and Brexit. She also met her future husband at a party event. They married in 2012 and have three children.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham said in an interview released Wednesday that Britain should consider options for its future relationship with the European Union, including ultimately rejoining the bloc, as he steps up efforts to rebuild ties with Europe.
Reuters
Since becoming leader, Ms. Badenoch has pulled the Conservatives further to the right in a bid to fend off Reform. She’s called for lower taxes, cuts to welfare spending and swift deportation of illegal immigrants.
She caused controversy last year by saying that “not all cultures are equally valid” when it comes to decid
